**Mesoscale News is reader-supported.** If you value independent reporting that connects climate science to what's happening in the world right now--and explains why it matters--please consider becoming a paid subscriber.
[Subscribe Now](https://substack.com/redirect/eb5252e3-efcc-4405-bf66-da0b37a90ce6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
[More than 1,000 people are dead](https://substack.com/redirect/b9916805-9224-45d1-b891-9bb79137a726?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after part of a glacier and mountainside in the Himalayas collapsed, unleashing a wall of ice, rock, mud and water through Nepal and Tibet. Thousands more remain missing.
Three months earlier, scientists had gathered with government officials in Kathmandu to talk about almost exactly this.
[Experts met with government officials in May](https://substack.com/redirect/de106d8b-f65c-4a39-b28a-786e08fa5a56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to discuss the growing danger from glaciers and glacial lakes along the shared Nepal-Tibet Himalayan border. They called for hazard mapping, monitoring, information-sharing, and[ early-warning systems.](https://substack.com/redirect/af0cead3-750a-4768-b9d7-e854cf3d63ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
By the time the mountain came down in late August, those warning systems still did not exist.
There is a terrible simplicity to what happened next.
The mountain moved.
## This wasn't an ordinary flood
Calling what happened a "flood" almost understates it.
Most floods begin with water. Rain falls. Rivers rise. Meteorologists watch the storm on radar; gauges record rainfall and river levels; models estimate where the water will go. Even flash floods generally have an identifiable meteorological cause developing before the water arrives.
This disaster began with the ground itself giving way.
[Subscribe Now](https://substack.com/redirect/eb5252e3-efcc-4405-bf66-da0b37a90ce6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
On August 26, a huge mass near Langtang Lirung catastrophically failed. Early reports described a glacier collapse, but subsequent satellite analysis indicated that bedrock beneath the glacier failed with it.
An enormous section of mountain -- rock, ice and everything attached to it -- started falling.
The collapse released enough energy that seismic instruments initially registered what appeared to be an earthquake. The U.S. Geological Survey later concluded there had been no earthquake. The mountain falling apart had itself generated seismic energy equivalent to a magnitude 5.2 earthquake.
Gravity did the rest.
As the avalanche accelerated downhill, it collected soil, boulders, sediment, trees, ice and water. It entered streams and river channels and collected still more material. The narrow Himalayan valleys acted like a chute, concentrating all that mass and energy and directing it downstream.
The resulting debris flow traveled nearly 100 kilometers, destroying everything in its path.
One engineer assisting with the rescue effort estimated portions of it may have moved faster than 160 kilometers per hour.
That is the geographic reality of a disaster like this.
The sky doesn't have to be raining.
The river doesn't have to slowly rise.
The mountain can simply come down.
## Scientists saw the danger
That doesn't mean this was unforeseeable.
Scientists examining satellite imagery found changes on the glacier before the collapse. A rapid assessment by the scientific group HiRISK identified "pre-event indications" of instability.
Scientists had also spent years warning that the Hindu Kush Himalaya needed better monitoring and early-warning systems as its glaciers rapidly changed.
For people immediately below the collapse, there may have been little anyone could have done. When millions of tons of mountain begin moving above you, geography allows very little time for negotiation.
[Subscribe Now](https://substack.com/redirect/eb5252e3-efcc-4405-bf66-da0b37a90ce6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But geography also means the farther downstream you are, the more time exists between collapse and impact.
Scientists estimated some communities could have had ten minutes or more of warning. That doesn't sound like much until the alternative is zero.
Ten minutes is enough to leave a riverbank.
Ten minutes is enough to run uphill.
Ten minutes is enough to stop traffic from entering a bridge or evacuate workers from a hydropower facility.
Ten minutes can be the difference between a disaster and a mass casualty event.
Instead, the avalanche tore through a landscape increasingly crowded with infrastructure. Roads, bridges, villages, hydropower plants and workers' camps occupy the same narrow valleys through which gravity inevitably sends water, rock and ice.
Twelve hydropower facilities and a solar plant (together representing roughly 10% of Nepal's operational electricity capacity) were shut down after the disaster.
That is another lesson here: climate disasters rarely remain politely confined to one category.
A glacier collapses.
It becomes a landslide.
The landslide becomes a debris flow.
The debris flow becomes a flood.
The flood becomes an energy crisis, an infrastructure disaster and a humanitarian catastrophe.
[Subscribe Now](https://substack.com/redirect/eb5252e3-efcc-4405-bf66-da0b37a90ce6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## The mountains are changing
The underlying physics isn't a mystery.
The Himalayas are warming. Glaciers are retreating. Permafrost (the frozen material that can help bind high mountain slopes together) is thawing.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/066c8edf-f5e4-4090-87aa-3b0c7bb0c6fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Remove enough ice from fractures in a mountainside and you change its structural stability. Retreat a glacier and you remove enormous amounts of weight while exposing slopes that may not have been uncovered for centuries. Melt enough ice and water collects behind unstable natural dams, creating glacial lakes capable of bursting catastrophically.
Across the Hindu Kush Himalaya, glacier loss accelerated by 65% between the decades beginning in 2000 and 2010.
Even if humanity manages to keep warming below 2°C (a threshold we have already temporarily surpassed), researchers project the region's glaciers could lose roughly 30-50% of their volume by the end of this century. Under current emissions trajectories, losses could approach 80%.
And this isn't only Nepal's problem.
The Hindu Kush Himalaya is sometimes called Earth's "Third Pole" because of the enormous volume of ice stored there. Its snow and glaciers feed river systems that sustain communities across Asia.
What happens high in these mountains does not stay high in these mountains.
Neither does global warming.
We have spent decades talking about climate change as something coming toward us: a future crisis, measured in fractions of degrees and projections for 2050 or 2100. But the reality has always been the climate change is a disaster that is right here, right now, and does not have to only be measured in future possibilities.
Measure it in a glacier retreating up a valley.
Measure it in permafrost disappearing from the cracks holding a mountainside together.
Measure it in a river carrying boulders where, minutes earlier, people were working.
Measure it in the distance between a scientist's warning and a government's failure to act on it.
Because that may be the most damning part of what happened in Nepal and Tibet.
The mountain did not betray anyone.
The glacier did not ignore a warning.
Scientists identified the danger. They asked for monitoring. They asked for hazard maps. They asked for early-warning systems.
Then the climate kept warming.
The ice kept melting.
And we kept waiting.
Until heat and gravity answered for us.
* * *

body:
If you've been serious about changing Texas, you need to have eyes on this race...
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241047%2E444211%2EjaPvXR)
Tonight, I'm writing to you about our future Lieutenant Governor, my friend Vikki Goodwin.
Not everyone knows this, but the**Lieutenant Governor is the most powerful political position in Texas politics.** They co-write our multi-billion dollar state budget and set the legislative agenda in the Texas Senate. They decide committee appointments and control what bills get passed into law.
Dan Patrick has used that power to do favors for his donors at your expense.
One example? He took a $3 million bribe from a pro-Paxton PAC, then presided over Ken Paxton's impeachment trial. _Paxton walked free._
**There's no clearer example of corruption.**
Patrick has used the Lieutenant Governor's office to gut public school funding and force fellow Republicans to vote for the school vouchers against the will of their own voters. He voted twice for the tax incentives program that brought hundreds of data centers to Texas to use up your drinking water and is still taking campaign contributions from the industry.
**And most recently, he’s refusing to face Vikki in a debate — but he dropped his first attack ad against her last week.**
A decade of Dan Patrick’s leadership has given us civil rights rollbacks, skyrocketing cost of living, and a Senate that does favors for the wealthy instead of working for We the People.
_Enter Vikki Goodwin:_
She's a four-term state representative from Central Texas, a small business owner, and someone who has fought vouchers every single session. She authored Cati's Act. She's led on water. And unlike Dan Patrick, she can't be bought.
She flipped her seat in 2018 by out-organizing the incumbent Republican, and has made her district deep blue by listening to and delivering for her constituents.
To support Vikki's campaign, I'm asking you to help us hit $5,000 with this email. I know that might sound like a lot, but here's what it actually looks like:
50 people give $100 — we're there.
100 people give $50 — we're there.

I've watched Texas politics for a long time, and I know what's possible when people decide to fight.
Vikki is that person. She's ready. Make sure she has what she needs to fight for all of us.

Happy September, Team Thompson!
Sandra Larson here, Vern’s campaign manager.
**This year, Vern has put the office of Agriculture Commissioner in the spotlight like never before.**
You’ve seen the massive engagement he’s received on social media. And now [**the response he’s getting from news outlets across the state**](https://us.list-manage.com/j3rQHnqmrON?e=37dda778f5&c2id=cdbf6368064ed4acbe3dc3fec7c073dc).
Vern’s message is resonating with North Dakotans. People are showing up.
And with each passing month, that many new, first-time donors contribute to amplify Vern’s message. August gave our campaign a major shot in the arm; people are listening and chipping in. But we need to do more in these final two full months before Election Day.
If you haven’t yet donated, now is the time- [**Will you help us kick off September with a first-time donation to reach our goal of 100 new donors for the month?**](https://us.list-manage.com/gDJAL5BKuBo?e=37dda778f5&c2id=cdbf6368064ed4acbe3dc3fec7c073dc)
If you have already donated, thank you! Your support means the world to Vern. And please feel free to share this email with others who might want to become a first-time donor!
Together, we’ve got this.Sandra LarsonCampaign ManagerThompson4ND

| | Join Kimberly Fletcher, President of Moms for America, and special guests Aly Legge, Amy Robbins, and Tyler Ohta for a powerful conversation from the Freedom Stage at the Great American State Fair. Inspired by Kimberly Fletcher’s Remembering the Ladies, this special live episode celebrates the courageous women who helped shape America—from the Founding Mothers and suffragists to the patriotic women carrying their legacy forward today. Courage. Legacy. Patriotism. Remembering the Ladies. Listen in for an inspiring conversation about the women who came before us and the responsibility we share to keep their stories—and the American story—alive. Full episode available now on [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/4bQ0_--FA/c?w=Q8DKlIE2bvFKSSArvEXtlguUlB8jiLUW1Iw7tBklU7Q.), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/4bQ0_--FA/c?w=xK2P1RgfB8cACN74cuEv1VEecj_5OX0BIkKqxIlnPJY.), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/4bQ0_--FA/c?w=gDKNI4iHr9KHqq45lOzCP4qhdr6AfehZIIuEjDKev8Y.) and [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/4bQ0_--FA/c?w=FYZRQKgv-1QInJn2f-NvhMb-yhQ7-4M4uziFl52gJNU.).

| | What does it take to make history? Not necessarily fame, wealth, or a powerful position. Some of history’s most influential women were ordinary people who saw a need and chose to act. Irena Sendler risked her life to rescue children during the Holocaust. Harriet Beecher Stowe used her writing to awaken hearts about slavery. Wai Jia Tam, at just 18, worked to provide a permanent home for vulnerable girls in Nepal. And Kimberly Fletcher, a mom of eight, turned a burden on her heart into a grassroots movement that became Moms for America. None knew where their first steps would lead. They simply acted with courage. And mama, you can too. You don’t have to change the world today. Teach your children, speak up, gather moms to pray, or serve your community. Your choices today are shaping generations to come! Read the [full blog](https://momsforamerica.us/so/4bQ0_--FA/c?w=LIkxw6QWtzle0DaeCwFaq4QoD0osiYs-CSuSmKGeAKs.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubW9tc2ZvcmFtZXJpY2EudXMvYmxvZyIsInIiOiJiZGVjNGNjNi02NTVhLTRhNGEtYjAxOC00YmFmZDFjMmVmYWEiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ) and discover how five courageous women, and you, can make a difference.

name: Jocelyn Benson
subject: We’re about to hit Mile 25
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/14280?t=1001&akid=1834%2E181023%2EqfCc6R ]A selfie of Jocelyn Benson in front of a wall covered in Benson for
Governor yard signs.

Hi, today I
wanted to send a different kind of email.

I’m checking in from the office between campaign stops — and my team just
let me know the results of our end-of-month fundraising deadline.

And I’m so grateful to say... we CRUSHED our goal!

This wouldn’t have been possible without the support of
supporters like
you. From the bottom of my heart, thank you!

When I say this campaign is built on grassroots support, I mean it. Our
average gift for August was $31. I know that sounds like a lot — and it
is! — but compared to the $6 million checks my opponent gets regularly,
we’re building a very different kind of movement.

We’re officially entering the final stretch of this election. The next
month is going to be a lot like Mile 25. Pardon the marathon metaphor, but
it’s true – you’re exhausted and you’re ready to quit, but the finish line
is right there.

This is what we’ve been training for. From now until Election
Day, everyone on Team Benson-Brinks is going to be running at full speed,

They thought you were too busy or too exhausted by the news cycle to put up a fight. They severely miscalculated. Today is September 1st, which means we have exactly two months until Election Day. We have 60 days to take the fight directly into the home districts of the politicians targeting our public lands and hold them accountable at the ballot box. We are going to put their voting records on blast. We are going to make sure every hunter, angler, hiker, and voter knows exactly who rubber-stamped the selloff of our national heritage for a quick buck. We aren't going to let them hide behind their PR spin; we are going to make this corporate land grab a massive electoral liability. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after feud with War Secretary Pete Hegseth. Kalshi suspends GOP House candidate Laurie Buckhout for betting on her own race. # Iran
* **Tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz:**
* A tanker was [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/4ec927b6-c2b1-44ea-9296-0e348b0bdd44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by three unidentified projectiles while completing an outbound transit through the Strait of Hormuz, UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on Monday. The attack occurred 17 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman. No casualties or environmental damage were reported.
* Separately, the UKMTO [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/1cec22fd-4f17-4f21-b848-7677a30f1b1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) earlier on Monday that it received a report from a tanker's master of another incident involving a vessel and military forces in the Indian Ocean, off Oman. UKMTO did not identify the tanker or military force involved, nor whether anyone was injured or the vessel was damaged.

* **Death toll from U.S. attack on Larak Island rises to three:** The death toll from the U.S. attack on Iran's Larak Island rose to three on Monday, after a person succumbed to their injuries in hospital, according to the Tasnim news agency.

* **IRGC claims it shot down U.S. MQ-9 drone over Strait of Hormuz:** Iran's IRGC said its air defences intercepted a U.S. MQ-9 drone in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to a statement carried by Iranian broadcaster Press TV.
* **Iran says U.S. must fulfill MOU commitments, Tehran will "immediately" reciprocate: **Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan that "the U.S. must return to its commitments and abide by the terms of the memorandum. Only then can we move out of the current situation, as all countries are concerned about bringing the war to an end as soon as possible."
* Iran will "immediately" reciprocate if the U.S. fulfills its commitments under the MOU, Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian said.
* Signed in June, the Pakistan-brokered memorandum is an interim agreement that expired on August 17.

* **Trump strikes aggressive tone on Iran, claims U.S. control over Hormuz, reportedly mulls more strikes:** In a series of remarks on Monday, U.S. President Donald Trump [told](https://substack.com/redirect/5d8bec6c-8462-4776-ad74-482712f4579e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reporters that the U.S. was pondering further attacks on Iran and that it remains in control of the Strait.
* He called Iran a "failed nation" in remarks at the White House on Monday morning, and claimed that the U.S. would still "smack them" in response to Iran's retaliatory strikes on U.S. bases in Jordan and strike on the UAE.
* He also said that the Strait of Hormuz was in "extremely good shape", claiming that the U.S. Navy is assisting the movement of an average of "30 ships a night."
* When [asked](https://substack.com/redirect/3bfcec82-ee27-4672-816d-ff6567f3a432?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by a reporter in the Oval Office if he had "ruled out using a nuclear weapon against Iran," Trump responded that he would "never say that, but the answer is yes," claiming that such an attack would be unnecessary, given that Iran had already been "totally defeated militarily."
* White House spokesperson Kush Desai told Al Jazeera that the president is keeping all of his options regarding Iran open, and that "he's willing to use every tool at his disposal," with Desai noting that the economic tools presently in use are "very powerful."
* Axios reported on Monday that Trump is [considering](https://substack.com/redirect/a568588b-cccb-4aa5-af8b-cd50b43e2c57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a CENTCOM plan for periodic strikes on Iranian radar, air-defense and anti-ship missile sites around the Strait of Hormuz. The proposal, backed by War Secretary Hegseth, is intended to prevent Iran from rebuilding its capacity to attack ships.
* **Bessent says sanctions meant to force Iran to "come to the table": **U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [told](https://substack.com/redirect/f9a2b73f-74e6-43e5-b82a-d692b8306bcd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) CNBC on Monday that the goal of United States sanctions on Iran is "to create the conditions that they will want to come to the table" for negotiations.
* Bessent told the Associated Press on Monday that the U.S. plans to impose sanctions on another Iranian bank this week as part of its economic campaign against Iran, though he declined to name the bank.
* Bessent also [reiterated](https://substack.com/redirect/a6182603-a8b7-4c6e-85ca-ba141b2e902e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the U.S. conditions for a deal with Iran, saying that Iran has to "give up their nuclear program," "turn over the highly-enriched uranium," "stop their support of proxies" and open the Strait of Hormuz.
* Bessent also suggested that the U.S. blockade had severely impaired Iran's oil industry, reducing Iranian oil remaining on the water to just 30 million barrels, far below Kpler's August 21 estimate of roughly 80 million barrels in floating storage outside the blockade zone. He argued that even if China keeps sending Iran payments for oil already sold, "that's going to run out" soon.
* **U.S. military commanders call Iran war "unsustainable":** Four senior U.S. commanders formally [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/71da5a1e-8171-4d27-8384-a6c5b5b0c5dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) War Secretary Pete Hegseth that the prolonged Iran operation is unsustainable and is already weakening the military's ability to confront threats elsewhere, including threats to the U.S. homeland, according to the Washington Post.
* The objections appeared in a classified August 14 assessment covering the worldwide availability of U.S. forces and weapons.
* Those involved in the warning include the Navy's top admiral, Daryl Caudle, and the commanders of the European, Southern, and Indo-Pacific commands.
* Caudle reportedly warned Hegseth that the Navy cannot maintain its current support for the war indefinitely, with barely one-quarter of the destroyer fleet reportedly ready to deploy.
* The Pentagon attacked the publication of the classified information but did not deny that the commanders filed formal objections.
* **U.S. announces deals to make missile interceptors:** The U.S. Department of War [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/bb5cde70-dc10-4417-8108-4fee9ee37923?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new seven-year agreements with General Dynamics and Lockheed Martin to triple production capacity for PAC-3 MSE interceptors, used by the Patriot air-defense system, and to quadruple capacity for THAAD interceptors.
* The Pentagon is committing to minimum annual purchases over the seven-year period. Congress will still have to approve the funding each year.

* **Kurdish group reportedly attacks Iranians in region bordering Iraq:** Fighters reportedly belonging to the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) attacked Iranian villagers in a western province bordering Iraq on Monday, Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency reported. An IRGC base in the same village was attacked by the group in 2018, according to Mehr.
* **Iran calls upon UN Security Council to intervene after U.S. attack on Larak Island:** In a letter to UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres on Monday, Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran's deputy permanent representative and ambassador to the UN, called for the UN Security Council to intervene after a U.S. attack on Larak Island killed and wounded soldiers and civilians, according to Iran's IRNA news agency.
* Darzi said in the letter that the attack was in "a clear violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity" of Iran, and accused the U.S. of war crimes and crimes against humanity.
* The letter asked the council to demand the U.S. end its attacks.

* **Asian fuel imports fall to lowest level since Iran war began:** Asia's imports of refined fuels have fallen to their lowest level since the U.S.-Iran war, Reuters reported on Monday, as supplies from the Gulf region have remained constrained as a result of the conflict over the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. blockade of Iran.
* The region, which consumes about 90 percent of Middle East crude, has cut its imports by nearly 4 million barrels a day and is depleting its inventories.
* Imports of light and middle distillates fell to an estimated 5.10 million barrels per day (bpd) in August, down from 5.61 million bpd in July, according to data compiled by the commodities analyst Kpler and cited by Reuters.
* Before the U.S. and Israel began attacks on Iran in February, the region's three-month average stood at 7.06 million bpd. The shortfall matches almost exactly the volume lost from the Middle East.

* Israeli naval forces opened fire on fishing boats and [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/51d636cd-dd1d-4d3b-9d32-7f12a847daf8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 10 fishermen off Al-Zawayda and Sheikh Ajlin, according to the Union of Fishermen's Committees.
* **Report: 2,030 Israeli army and settler attacks in occupied West Bank in August:** Israeli forces and settlers carried out 2,030 attacks against Palestinians, their land and property across the occupied West Bank in August, according to a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/a21725f0-12d9-4f6c-bede-31e84daf35a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) released Tuesday by the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. The settlers reportedly hit the mother in the head with clubs and stones, and pepper-sprayed the 10-year-old in the face, and raided another family home in the area, assaulting the women and children inside.

* **WFP halves food assistance in West Bank as needs rise:** The World Food Programme [said](https://substack.com/redirect/fd9a95fe-7dc4-4488-874e-fa1bda38a1b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday that funding shortages are forcing it to halve food assistance in the occupied West Bank from 400,000 to 200,000 people starting this month, even as Israeli military operations, settler violence, movement restrictions, demolitions, and displacement drive growing food insecurity. "At a time when WFP should be scaling up assistance to reach more people, we are being forced to make difficult decisions, prioritizing the most vulnerable while cutting assistance to others despite widespread needs," Shaun Hughes, WFP Country Director for Palestine, said in a statement.

* **Israel to return body of Palestinian 15-year-old it killed and held for nine months to family:** Israel's General Authority of Civil Affairs [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/3ded4eed-c915-4f5e-9781-116cf6271975?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that the body of 15-year-old Jadallah Jihad Juma Jadallah, from Al-Fara'a refugee camp in Tubas, whom Israeli forces shot and killed nine months ago, would be handed over to his family on Thursday.

* **Palestinian female detainees describe harsh conditions, medical neglect in Israeli prisons** : Palestinian female detainees [held](https://substack.com/redirect/446fcb7e-0a97-49e2-a792-5edaf929ec81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at Israel's Damon Prison and other facilities are enduring overcrowding, medical neglect, poor food, and punitive raids, according to a Monday statement from Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs.

* **British activist detained by settlers to be deported from Israel:** Finn Joughin, a British activist [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/f8317dce-79a4-4840-bcec-c4f940be716f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Saturday by armed Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank village of Umm al-Kheir and handed over to police, is set to be deported from Israel after UK embassy officials raised his case with Israeli authorities, according to The Times of Israel.

* Joughin's lawyer noted this, and said Joughin was attempting to prevent settlers from dismantling a fence and damaging property in a Palestinian village. He also noted that police did not question the settlers who detained Joughin.
* Joughin's case follows Israel's deportation of dozens of foreign activists who have traveled to the occupied West Bank to protect Palestinians through "protective presence" work amid a surge in settler violence in the area.

# U.S. News
* **Whistleblower: USPS mail ballot plan could disenfranchise millions** : An anonymous federal official [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/402b6d03-e326-417a-9085-9e79067c9df1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a congressional disclosure that a rushed, insufficiently tested Postal Service portal could reject entire batches of mail ballots--potentially tens of thousands at a time--under a "zero-percent failure policy" if even a single sampled barcode fails to match voter data, Sen. **Richard Blumenthal** (D-Conn.) disclosed Tuesday.
* The newly designed system could thus prevent millions of Americans from receiving their ballots. "As designed, the process is entirely unforgiving," the disclosure notes.
* The whistleblower said the online portal was built under constantly shifting requirements with as few as four working days for customer testing before its planned launch.
* The system stems from President Donald Trump's executive order overhauling mail voting, which a federal judge has blocked for now. The Trump administration continues to pursue the order's reinstatement ahead of North Carolina's Friday ballot-mailing deadline.
* **Vance calls Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed "evil": **Vice President **JD Vance** described Democratic Senate nominee **Abdul El-Sayed** as "very, very evil" during a Monday rally in Sterling Heights, Michigan, hosted by the pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc., pointing to El-Sayed's recent apology over his response to a March synagogue attack and his alliance with Twitch streamer **Hasan Piker**.
* El-Sayed, who has been the subject of a wave of recent media attacks for his relationship with Piker, faces Republican **Mike Rogers** in November for the open seat currently held by Democrat **Gary Peters**.
* **Haitian college student dies in apparent suicide after losing TPS:** **Pierre Damas Bel** , a 20-year-old Haitian immigrant, walked into westbound Interstate 70 traffic in Springfield, Ohio Monday and was struck and [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/3cad7e1e-a784-4e41-af86-aa1ba2de485b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by a tractor-trailer in what his family believes was a suicide, according to The Washington Post.
* Bel had grown increasingly distraught following the loss of his temporary protected status. He had been fitted with an ICE ankle monitor as a result, with his father saying that Bel "felt like he was treated like an animal."
* Bel had written on Instagram in July, "now I'm walking through the streets of the United States with a GPS monitor on my leg, carrying a feeling of shame and humiliation that I never imagined I would experience."
* Bel, who arrived in the U.S. in 2024 to reunite with his parents and had graduated high school with honors while planning to study medicine, had a pending asylum claim with a hearing scheduled for October.
* **Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after feud with Hegseth:** U.S. Army Secretary **Dan Driscoll** has [submitted](https://substack.com/redirect/365e415a-bf73-4880-88bb-1a435f927739?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his resignation to President Trump and is expected to leave the Pentagon within days, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
* The Army's top civilian official and a close ally of Vice President **JD Vance** , Driscoll had reportedly clashed for months with War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** over the service's direction, blocked promotions, and Hegseth's removal of senior officers.
* His departure will leave the Army without either a Senate-confirmed civilian leader or a confirmed chief of staff.
* **Kalshi suspends GOP House candidate Buckhout for betting on her own race** : On Monday, the prediction market Kalshi [suspended](https://substack.com/redirect/ac873ef8-fabe-4c01-a994-ffe21161c5df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Republican House candidate **Laurie Buckhout,** running in a swing North Carolina district against Democratic incumbent **Don Davis** , for three years and fined her about $2,600 after finding she wagered less than $1,000 on her own race.
* Buckhout, a retired Army colonel who cooperated with the investigation, acknowledged the mistake, saying "I bet on myself. Literally."
* The action follows Kalshi's April suspension of three other congressional candidates who bet on their races and coincides with a Monday lifetime ban imposed on former Rep.**George Santos** for failing to cooperate with the company's investigation. Santos was fined earlier this year by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for insider trading tied to a bet on his own State of the Union attendance.
* **Trump asks Supreme Court to immediately fire 29 transgender service members** : The Trump administration [filed](https://substack.com/redirect/a3df7e4e-21f7-4239-8940-f36e29a0105b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an urgent Supreme Court appeal seeking the immediate removal of 29 active-duty transgender service members before their case challenging the Pentagon's transgender ban goes to trial in January, calling it a matter of "exceptional importance."
* Solicitor General **John Sauer** called a lower court ruling that blocked the military from discharging the plaintiffs in U.S. v. Talbott "gravely erroneous."
* The justices will decide this fall whether the Supreme Court will hear the case.
* **FTC sues Amazon over alleged secret ad price manipulation:** The Federal Trade Commission and more than 20 state attorneys general [sued](https://substack.com/redirect/fc8e7303-b0a7-44ad-a6b7-352c25122b20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Amazon Monday, alleging the company secretly manipulated advertising auctions to raise prices for businesses advertising on its platform, generating tens of billions of dollars over seven years while costing advertisers more than $20 billion.
* The lawsuit alleges Amazon began entering its own bids in auctions starting in 2018--internally called a "soft reserve"--without disclosing the practice to advertisers.
* The FTC claims Amazon intervened in 70%-80% of auctions in recent years and raised pay-per-click costs by 50% on major shopping days.
* This will be the FTC's third major case against the company.

* **U.S. progressives join hemispheric "anti-CPAC" summit pushing back on Trump's Latin America agenda: **Congressional candidates **Adam Hamawy** , **Chris Rabb** , and New Yorkers **Claire Valdez** and **Darializa Avila Chevalier** were [part](https://substack.com/redirect/83e93348-5bf8-4d60-b1a4-2366a93a903e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of a U.S. progressive delegation that attended the third Pan-American Congress in Montevideo, Uruguay from Friday to Sunday, a parliamentary forum of left and progressive forces from across the Americas.
* The gathering drew more than 150 lawmakers, former presidents, and political figures from 15 countries, including former Chilean President **Gabriel Boric** and Uruguayan Vice President **Carolina Cosse.**
* Organizers characterized it as a counterweight to the right-wing CPAC network that helped elevate leaders like**Javier Milei** , and to what critics call Trump's "Donroe Doctrine" of militarized intervention in the region.
* The U.S. delegation was led by Reps. **Pramila Jayapal** and Jesus **" Chuy" Garcia.**
* Participants denounced U.S. interference in the region while calling for a foreign policy "rooted in multilateralism, cooperation, and respect for the sovereignty of all nations," Hamawy said.

* **Three minors killed in Colombian military strike on FARC dissidents** : A Colombian military air strike on August 27 in southern Guaviare department [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/edc06df2-9549-4830-acd4-367252af3db0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 10 people, including three minors aged 15 and 16, targeting a dissident faction of the former FARC rebel group, according to the country's National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences and the Ministry of National Defense.
* President Abelardo de la Espriella, a right-wing ally of Donald Trump who took office earlier this month, said the strike was part of intensified operations against armed groups and wrote on X that "the bandits, who for decades have recruited minors to turn them into combatants or human shields, must pay for these crimes."
* **India rejects international court ruling on Indus Waters Treaty** : India [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/fc3a7143-12c4-4841-b856-4d50d60d361c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Monday ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration ordering it to uphold the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan, with the Ministry of External Affairs saying the tribunal has "no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India's sovereign decisions."
* India suspended the treaty in April last year, following an attack on a village in Kashmir that killed 26 people, in which two of three assailants were later identified by Indian authorities as Pakistani nationals. Pakistan has denied involvement in the incident.
* The tribunal, which is housed at the Hague, ruled that the treaty remains fully binding, ordered India to limit construction on the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant in Kashmir, and restricted work on the dam wall and power intake structure above certain levels.
* The restrictions are expected to remain in place until 90 days after a World Bank-appointed neutral expert issues a decision in the case, which is expected by July 2027.
* **Eurasian leaders gather for Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Kyrgyzstan:** The leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's 10 member states--China, Russia, India, Iran, Pakistan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan--[gathered](https://substack.com/redirect/cd0f0c36-464e-44c7-9d7b-9a41fa44cd90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Kyrgyzstan alongside representatives of numerous partner countries for a summit intended to deepen cooperation among non-Western powers.
* Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended alongside Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and leaders from across Central Asia. Putin held separate meetings with Xi and Modi and is expected to meet Pezeshkian on Tuesday.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz: A tanker was by three unidentified projectiles while completing an outbound transit through the Strait of Hormuz, UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on Monday. The attack occurred 17 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman. No casualties or environmental damage were reported. Separately, the UKMTO earlier on Monday that it received a report from a tanker's master of another incident involving a vessel and military forces in the Indian Ocean, off Oman. UKMTO did not identify the tanker or military force involved, nor whether anyone was injured or the vessel was damaged. Death toll from U.S. attack on Larak Island rises to three: The death toll from the U.S. attack on Iran's Larak Island rose to three on Monday, after a person succumbed to their injuries in hospital, according to the Tasnim news agency. IRGC claims it shot down U.S. MQ-9 drone over Strait of Hormuz: Iran's IRGC said its air defences intercepted a U.S. MQ-9 drone in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to a statement carried by Iranian broadcaster Press TV. Iran says U.S. must fulfill MOU commitments, Tehran will "immediately" reciprocate: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan that "the U.S. must return to its commitments and abide by the terms of the memorandum. Only then can we move out of the current situation, as all countries are concerned about bringing the war to an end as soon as possible." Iran will "immediately" reciprocate if the U.S. fulfills its commitments under the MOU, Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian said. Signed in June, the Pakistan-brokered memorandum is an interim agreement that expired on August 17. Trump strikes aggressive tone on Iran, claims U.S. control over Hormuz, reportedly mulls more strikes: In a series of remarks on Monday, U.S. President Donald Trump reporters that the U.S. was pondering further attacks on Iran and that it remains in control of the Strait. He called Iran a "failed nation" in remarks at the White House on Monday morning, and claimed that the U.S. would still "smack them" in response to Iran's retaliatory strikes on U.S. bases in Jordan and strike on the UAE. He also said that the Strait of Hormuz was in "extremely good shape", claiming that the U.S. Navy is assisting the movement of an average of "30 ships a night." When by a reporter in the Oval Office if he had "ruled out using a nuclear weapon against Iran," Trump responded that he would "never say that, but the answer is yes," claiming that such an attack would be unnecessary, given that Iran had already been "totally defeated militarily." White House spokesperson Kush Desai told Al Jazeera that the president is keeping all of his options regarding Iran open, and that "he's willing to use every tool at his disposal," with Desai noting that the economic tools presently in use are "very powerful." Axios reported on Monday that Trump is a CENTCOM plan for periodic strikes on Iranian radar, air-defense and anti-ship missile sites around the Strait of Hormuz. The proposal, backed by War Secretary Hegseth, is intended to prevent Iran from rebuilding its capacity to attack ships. Bessent says sanctions meant to force Iran to "come to the table": U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent CNBC on Monday that the goal of United States sanctions on Iran is "to create the conditions that they will want to come to the table" for negotiations. Bessent told the Associated Press on Monday that the U.S. plans to impose sanctions on another Iranian bank this week as part of its economic campaign against Iran, though he declined to name the bank. Bessent also the U.S. conditions for a deal with Iran, saying that Iran has to "give up their nuclear program," "turn over the highly-enriched uranium," "stop their support of proxies" and open the Strait of Hormuz. Bessent also suggested that the U.S. blockade had severely impaired Iran's oil industry, reducing Iranian oil remaining on the water to just 30 million barrels, far below Kpler's August 21 estimate of roughly 80 million barrels in floating storage outside the blockade zone. He argued that even if China keeps sending Iran payments for oil already sold, "that's going to run out" soon. U.S. military commanders call Iran war "unsustainable": Four senior U.S. commanders formally War Secretary Pete Hegseth that the prolonged Iran operation is unsustainable and is already weakening the military's ability to confront threats elsewhere, including threats to the U.S. homeland, according to the Washington Post. The objections appeared in a classified August 14 assessment covering the worldwide availability of U.S. forces and weapons. Those involved in the warning include the Navy's top admiral, Daryl Caudle, and the commanders of the European, Southern, and Indo-Pacific commands. Caudle reportedly warned Hegseth that the Navy cannot maintain its current support for the war indefinitely, with barely one-quarter of the destroyer fleet reportedly ready to deploy. The Pentagon attacked the publication of the classified information but did not deny that the commanders filed formal objections. U.S. announces deals to make missile interceptors: The U.S. Department of War new seven-year agreements with General Dynamics and Lockheed Martin to triple production capacity for PAC-3 MSE interceptors, used by the Patriot air-defense system, and to quadruple capacity for THAAD interceptors. The Pentagon is committing to minimum annual purchases over the seven-year period. Congress will still have to approve the funding each year. Kurdish group reportedly attacks Iranians in region bordering Iraq: Fighters reportedly belonging to the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) attacked Iranian villagers in a western province bordering Iraq on Monday, Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency reported. An IRGC base in the same village was attacked by the group in 2018, according to Mehr. Iran calls upon UN Security Council to intervene after U.S. attack on Larak Island: In a letter to UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres on Monday, Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran's deputy permanent representative and ambassador to the UN, called for the UN Security Council to intervene after a U.S. attack on Larak Island killed and wounded soldiers and civilians, according to Iran's IRNA news agency. Darzi said in the letter that the attack was in "a clear violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity" of Iran, and accused the U.S. of war crimes and crimes against humanity. The letter asked the council to demand the U.S. end its attacks. Asian fuel imports fall to lowest level since Iran war began: Asia's imports of refined fuels have fallen to their lowest level since the U.S.-Iran war, Reuters reported on Monday, as supplies from the Gulf region have remained constrained as a result of the conflict over the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. blockade of Iran. The region, which consumes about 90 percent of Middle East crude, has cut its imports by nearly 4 million barrels a day and is depleting its inventories. Imports of light and middle distillates fell to an estimated 5.10 million barrels per day (bpd) in August, down from 5.61 million bpd in July, according to data compiled by the commodities analyst Kpler and cited by Reuters. Before the U.S. and Israel began attacks on Iran in February, the region's three-month average stood at 7.06 million bpd. The shortfall matches almost exactly the volume lost from the Middle East. Yemen Saudi-backed Yemeni forces target Ansarallah positions, claim four drone boats destroyed in Red Sea: Yemen's Saudi-backed military said it carried out drone attacks on Ansarallah positions across several fronts, including targets in Baqam district in the northern Saada governorate. Separately, its navy said it destroyed four Ansarallah drone boats near the Hanish and Zuqar islands in the Red Sea. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, six Palestinians were killed and 13 were injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One Palestinian was killed in a building collapse, bringing the number of people killed in building collapses to 34. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,462 killed, with 174,509 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,326 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,398, while 815 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli attacks on Gaza kill seven, including two children: Israeli forces carried out heavy airstrikes and shelling in western Gaza City, killing four Palestinians, including two children and a woman, in the Al-Katiba area. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz later a senior Hamas member had been captured, without identifying him. The Israeli military confirmed striking "a number of targets," saying the attacks were intended to "remove threats to security forces." A resistance-affiliated security channel said the operation had targeted a senior Hamas figure but was thwarted, while acknowledging that an unnamed security official was abducted. It said the force behind the operation suffered losses and left behind weapons and equipment, and that three "collaborators" who had provided support and gathered intelligence were detained--members of Israeli-backed Palestinian militias were reportedly seen in the area at the time of the attack. Separately, two Palestinians were killed by Israeli gunfire west of Khan Younis, southern Gaza. A 73-year-old Palestinian man also died from a gunshot wound sustained earlier in Deir al-Balah. Gaza's Civil Defense said an Israeli strike critically wounded an officer and caused the amputation of parts of his limbs. Israeli naval forces opened fire on fishing boats and 10 fishermen off Al-Zawayda and Sheikh Ajlin, according to the Union of Fishermen's Committees. Report: 2,030 Israeli army and settler attacks in occupied West Bank in August: Israeli forces and settlers carried out 2,030 attacks against Palestinians, their land and property across the occupied West Bank in August, according to a released Tuesday by the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. The commission recorded 1,402 attacks by Israeli forces and 628 by settlers, saying the attacks were concentrated in areas facing intensified settlement expansion and growing efforts to control roads, movement routes, and agricultural and grazing land. Attacks continued on Monday and Tuesday: Ramallah : Israeli settlers severely beat an elderly Palestinian woman as she and her husband resisted an attempt to steal their livestock in the village of Burqa, according to Al Jazeera Arabic. In a separate attack on Monday evening, Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli soldiers, Burqa, injuring another Palestinian and her 10-year-old son. The settlers reportedly hit the mother in the head with clubs and stones, and pepper-sprayed the 10-year-old in the face, and raided another family home in the area, assaulting the women and children inside. Nablus: Settlers to the Nur Al-Din Zengi Mosque in Bizzariya, northwest of Nablus, setting a nearby room ablaze after failing to break down the mosque's doors and spray-painting racist slogans. Separately, Israeli forces beat and injured a young Palestinian man during a raid on Nablus's Old City. Bethlehem: Israeli settlers to a vehicle and spray-painted racist slogans on the wall of a home in the Bakoush area of Nahalin, west of Bethlehem, WAFA reported. WFP halves food assistance in West Bank as needs rise: The World Food Programme Tuesday that funding shortages are forcing it to halve food assistance in the occupied West Bank from 400,000 to 200,000 people starting this month, even as Israeli military operations, settler violence, movement restrictions, demolitions, and displacement drive growing food insecurity. "At a time when WFP should be scaling up assistance to reach more people, we are being forced to make difficult decisions, prioritizing the most vulnerable while cutting assistance to others despite widespread needs," Shaun Hughes, WFP Country Director for Palestine, said in a statement. WFP warned that funding shortages are also affecting assistance to 1.5 million people in Gaza and that further cuts will be unavoidable without additional funding. Israel to return body of Palestinian 15-year-old it killed and held for nine months to family: Israel's General Authority of Civil Affairs on Monday that the body of 15-year-old Jadallah Jihad Juma Jadallah, from Al-Fara'a refugee camp in Tubas, whom Israeli forces shot and killed nine months ago, would be handed over to his family on Thursday. Palestinian female detainees describe harsh conditions, medical neglect in Israeli prisons : Palestinian female detainees at Israel's Damon Prison and other facilities are enduring overcrowding, medical neglect, poor food, and punitive raids, according to a Monday statement from Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs. The Commission cited several cases, including that of Abeer Odeh, a detainee with a history of respiratory issues who has developed scabies while receiving only partial medical treatment, and Yasmeen Shaaban, who suffered a uterine injury from beatings and has been unable to receive a needed surgery since her re-detention in May 2025; the Commission said roughly 92 Palestinian women are currently held in Israeli detention. The Commission noted National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir raided the prison on August 19 and "boasted of being directly responsible for imposing restrictions" on detainees. Netanyahu touts ability to 'influence' U.S. politicians and media in reelection campaign: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is campaigning for reelection by touting his ability to influence U.S. politics and media, pointing to his role in bringing Washington around during the war with Iran. Speaking to Israel's Channel 14, Netanyahu , "It took a long time to bring the United States to its senses. I could do it," citing "close to 1,000 hours on American television," his "intimate knowledge" of U.S. leaders, and his "ability to influence the United States" and "navigate this field." British activist detained by settlers to be deported from Israel: Finn Joughin, a British activist Saturday by armed Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank village of Umm al-Kheir and handed over to police, is set to be deported from Israel after UK embassy officials raised his case with Israeli authorities, according to The Times of Israel. Settlers accused Joughin of assaulting an Israeli minor during his work in the village. He can be seen in video footage of the attack pressing his body against that of an Israeli minor in an apparent attempt to prevent the minor from passing through to a Palestinian home. Joughin's lawyer noted this, and said Joughin was attempting to prevent settlers from dismantling a fence and damaging property in a Palestinian village. He also noted that police did not question the settlers who detained Joughin. Joughin's case follows Israel's deportation of dozens of foreign activists who have traveled to the occupied West Bank to protect Palestinians through "protective presence" work amid a surge in settler violence in the area. Lebanon Israeli forces demolish homes and set off explosions in southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire":Israeli vehicles further into Al-Mansouri, in the Tyre (Sour) district Tuesday and demolished several homes, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported. In Bint Jbeil district, Israeli forces set off a powerful explosion in Rshaf. On Monday, Israeli forces used illegal white phosphorus munitions in attacks on villages in Nabatieh, according to the NNA. In Nabatieh, a child from wounds sustained when unexploded Israeli ordnance detonated in Habboush on Monday, also wounding another boy. Ibrahim's father had previously been killed in an Israeli attack on southern Lebanon. U.S. News Whistleblower: USPS mail ballot plan could disenfranchise millions : An anonymous federal official in a congressional disclosure that a rushed, insufficiently tested Postal Service portal could reject entire batches of mail ballots--potentially tens of thousands at a time--under a "zero-percent failure policy" if even a single sampled barcode fails to match voter data, Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) disclosed Tuesday. The newly designed system could thus prevent millions of Americans from receiving their ballots. "As designed, the process is entirely unforgiving," the disclosure notes. The whistleblower said the online portal was built under constantly shifting requirements with as few as four working days for customer testing before its planned launch. The system stems from President Donald Trump's executive order overhauling mail voting, which a federal judge has blocked for now. The Trump administration continues to pursue the order's reinstatement ahead of North Carolina's Friday ballot-mailing deadline. Vance calls Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed "evil": Vice President JD Vance described Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed as "very, very evil" during a Monday rally in Sterling Heights, Michigan, hosted by the pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc., pointing to El-Sayed's recent apology over his response to a March synagogue attack and his alliance with Twitch streamer Hasan Piker. El-Sayed, who has been the subject of a wave of recent media attacks for his relationship with Piker, faces Republican Mike Rogers in November for the open seat currently held by Democrat Gary Peters. Haitian college student dies in apparent suicide after losing TPS: Pierre Damas Bel , a 20-year-old Haitian immigrant, walked into westbound Interstate 70 traffic in Springfield, Ohio Monday and was struck and by a tractor-trailer in what his family believes was a suicide, according to The Washington Post. Bel had grown increasingly distraught following the loss of his temporary protected status. He had been fitted with an ICE ankle monitor as a result, with his father saying that Bel "felt like he was treated like an animal." Bel had written on Instagram in July, "now I'm walking through the streets of the United States with a GPS monitor on my leg, carrying a feeling of shame and humiliation that I never imagined I would experience." Bel, who arrived in the U.S. in 2024 to reunite with his parents and had graduated high school with honors while planning to study medicine, had a pending asylum claim with a hearing scheduled for October. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after feud with Hegseth: U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has his resignation to President Trump and is expected to leave the Pentagon within days, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday. The Army's top civilian official and a close ally of Vice President JD Vance , Driscoll had reportedly clashed for months with War Secretary Pete Hegseth over the service's direction, blocked promotions, and Hegseth's removal of senior officers. His departure will leave the Army without either a Senate-confirmed civilian leader or a confirmed chief of staff. Kalshi suspends GOP House candidate Buckhout for betting on her own race : On Monday, the prediction market Kalshi Republican House candidate Laurie Buckhout, running in a swing North Carolina district against Democratic incumbent Don Davis , for three years and fined her about $2,600 after finding she wagered less than $1,000 on her own race. Buckhout, a retired Army colonel who cooperated with the investigation, acknowledged the mistake, saying "I bet on myself. Literally." The action follows Kalshi's April suspension of three other congressional candidates who bet on their races and coincides with a Monday lifetime ban imposed on former Rep.George Santos for failing to cooperate with the company's investigation. Santos was fined earlier this year by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for insider trading tied to a bet on his own State of the Union attendance. Trump asks Supreme Court to immediately fire 29 transgender service members : The Trump administration an urgent Supreme Court appeal seeking the immediate removal of 29 active-duty transgender service members before their case challenging the Pentagon's transgender ban goes to trial in January, calling it a matter of "exceptional importance." Solicitor General John Sauer called a lower court ruling that blocked the military from discharging the plaintiffs in U.S. v. Talbott "gravely erroneous." The justices will decide this fall whether the Supreme Court will hear the case. FTC sues Amazon over alleged secret ad price manipulation: The Federal Trade Commission and more than 20 state attorneys general Amazon Monday, alleging the company secretly manipulated advertising auctions to raise prices for businesses advertising on its platform, generating tens of billions of dollars over seven years while costing advertisers more than $20 billion. The lawsuit alleges Amazon began entering its own bids in auctions starting in 2018--internally called a "soft reserve"--without disclosing the practice to advertisers. The FTC claims Amazon intervened in 70%-80% of auctions in recent years and raised pay-per-click costs by 50% on major shopping days. This will be the FTC's third major case against the company. U.S. progressives join hemispheric "anti-CPAC" summit pushing back on Trump's Latin America agenda: Congressional candidates Adam Hamawy , Chris Rabb , and New Yorkers Claire Valdez and Darializa Avila Chevalier were of a U.S. progressive delegation that attended the third Pan-American Congress in Montevideo, Uruguay from Friday to Sunday, a parliamentary forum of left and progressive forces from across the Americas. The gathering drew more than 150 lawmakers, former presidents, and political figures from 15 countries, including former Chilean President Gabriel Boric and Uruguayan Vice President Carolina Cosse. Organizers characterized it as a counterweight to the right-wing CPAC network that helped elevate leaders likeJavier Milei , and to what critics call Trump's "Donroe Doctrine" of militarized intervention in the region. The U.S. delegation was led by Reps. Pramila Jayapal and Jesus " Chuy" Garcia. Participants denounced U.S. interference in the region while calling for a foreign policy "rooted in multilateralism, cooperation, and respect for the sovereignty of all nations," Hamawy said. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News DRC Ebola outbreak becomes country 's worst, with over 6,000 cases and nearly 3,000 deaths: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has all previous surges to become the country's worst ever, with 6,041 confirmed cases and 2,911 deaths, according to the DRC Ministry of Communication. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called it "the fastest-spreading Ebola epidemic ever recorded." There is currently no approved vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain driving the outbreak. The response faces compounding challenges in the country's eastern provinces where fighting, displacement, and pre-existing humanitarian crises complicate care. Death toll from Nepal flood passes 1,000: The official death toll from Nepal's August 26 flash flood reached 1,050. More than 4,000 people remained missing, while at least 639 people were stranded at hydropower stations. According to Prime Minister Balendra Shah, More than 11,000 people have been rescued, Reuters . Russia strikes Ukrainian export and energy infrastructure near Romanian border: Russian missiles and drones port facilities, a ferry crossing and energy infrastructure in Ukraine's Odessa region overnight, damaging export infrastructure and the Orlivka checkpoint on the Romanian border, according to Ukrainian officials. Ukraine's Naftogaz said the attack damaged main and auxiliary equipment at its Odessa combined heat-and-power plant, where debris-removal operations were underway. Russia has sharply intensified attacks on Odessa's export infrastructure in recent months, effectively blocking Black Sea ports that once handled 90% of Ukraine's exports. U.S. approves $800 million military helicopter sale to Iraq: The U.S. State Department approved an $800 million sale of Bell helicopters and related military equipment to Iraq, according to a statement issued on Monday. The department said that the principal contractor will be Bell-Textron of Fort Worth, Texas, and that the sale would "improve Iraq's capability to meet current and future threats." Three minors killed in Colombian military strike on FARC dissidents : A Colombian military air strike on August 27 in southern Guaviare department 10 people, including three minors aged 15 and 16, targeting a dissident faction of the former FARC rebel group, according to the country's National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences and the Ministry of National Defense. President Abelardo de la Espriella, a right-wing ally of Donald Trump who took office earlier this month, said the strike was part of intensified operations against armed groups and wrote on X that "the bandits, who for decades have recruited minors to turn them into combatants or human shields, must pay for these crimes." India rejects international court ruling on Indus Waters Treaty : India a Monday ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration ordering it to uphold the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan, with the Ministry of External Affairs saying the tribunal has "no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India's sovereign decisions." India suspended the treaty in April last year, following an attack on a village in Kashmir that killed 26 people, in which two of three assailants were later identified by Indian authorities as Pakistani nationals. Pakistan has denied involvement in the incident. The tribunal, which is housed at the Hague, ruled that the treaty remains fully binding, ordered India to limit construction on the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant in Kashmir, and restricted work on the dam wall and power intake structure above certain levels. The restrictions are expected to remain in place until 90 days after a World Bank-appointed neutral expert issues a decision in the case, which is expected by July 2027. Eurasian leaders gather for Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Kyrgyzstan: The leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's 10 member states--China, Russia, India, Iran, Pakistan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan-- in Kyrgyzstan alongside representatives of numerous partner countries for a summit intended to deepen cooperation among non-Western powers. Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended alongside Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and leaders from across Central Asia. Billionaires and special interests making millions on the backs of working families. Folks struggling to put food on the table and afford basic needs. Republicans taking away health care from everyday people to give more money and access to the richest folks in America.
**We have to fix what’s broken in Washington DC, and electing Roy in North Carolina is CRITICAL to making that happen.

name: The Dads Initiative w/ ParentsTogether
subject: The Dads Initiative’s Second Show: Cart Talk
body:
Two dads. Nine holes. Honest conversation.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/a9c71e9b0da0/the-dads-initiatives-second-show-cart-talk?e=7e921d898f)
---
| | | | Hi Peter,
When we launched **The Dads Initiative** , our aim was always to make shows for fathers with the types of content they already seek out online and enjoy, with stories about fatherhood that resonate. We started with men’s style content in our first show, Reset Mode.
---
**Today, I am thrilled to announce the launch of our second show, Cart Talk, for the dads who love golf.**
| [Check Out our New Show: Cart Talk](https://us.list-manage.com/9UnW3g4eaet?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)
---
| | Golf has a massive, devoted fanbase – millions of men play, watch, and talk about it, often with their own kids – and it already has a content ecosystem that reaches exactly the dads we're trying to serve.
It can also be a lot like fatherhood. Sometimes there are major mis-hits, and you need a mulligan – in parenting, it’s often accompanied by an apology and a commitment to learn from our mistakes and do better next time. As a golfer, you dream of the perfect round. As a dad, the perfect day with the kids, whatever that may be.

Plus, the game gives men room to be real with each other – as dads, as men, as friends.
Hosted by [**Company of Dads**](https://us.list-manage.com/13lYPMX7mL2?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) founder – and avid golfer – **Paul Sullivan, Cart Talk** follows two dads playing nine holes, having honest conversations about golf, life, and fatherhood.
It’s fun to watch, and not just if you love golf. (Though especially if you love golf.) The moments that surface are real and authentic reflections on how we show up for our families, and for each other.
Golf Digest Editorial Director [**Max Adler**](https://us.list-manage.com/1hwQmJMgrHL?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) lives and breathes golf, but it’s supremely relatable to hear him talking about navigating life as a father of 4, including a set of twins.
Likewise, author [**Tom Coyne**](https://us.list-manage.com/19PxW3LgUK6?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) spent years traveling the world to play and write about the most prestigious courses, but he talks about finally coming back home to buy a rundown golf course of his own, and how that new adventure allows him to connect with his family in a new way, as they go along the journey together.
At **The Dads Initiative** , we’re so excited to be telling these stories, and many more to come.
Find full episodes on [**YouTube**](https://us.list-manage.com/128TrTA3Rvz?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf), and additional content (including some fun golf challenges!) on [**Instagram**](https://us.list-manage.com/1ARiZ3qtRJX?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf), [**Facebook**](https://us.list-manage.com/bmasf4o_SOH?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf), and [**TikTok**](https://us.list-manage.com/Dlc8oTN2jNA?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf).

We’d love for you to check it out and follow the show.
The Dads Initiative @ParentsTogether
---
| | _**Updates From our Partners**_
[ _**The Daddying Film Festival & Forum (D3F) 2027 Call for Entries is rolling through the summer on FilmFreeway!**_](https://us.list-manage.com/HNlK5jfySvV?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)**** Submissions will be accepted through **November 23rd** , so, plenty of time to create your films or videos demonstrating the importance of having or being an involved Dad/dad figure, including Instagram Reels, TikToks, music and dance videos!
Since 2022, we've received submissions from **60+** countries and we're excited to present another amazing collection of the [**best daddying stories**](https://us.list-manage.com/StKwGmCVKNI?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) told by students (3rd grade-undergrad), Dads/Granddads, Moms/Grandmoms, dad figures, parenting podcasters, and indie filmmakers from around the world! Check the [**D3F website**](https://us.list-manage.com/NVshDPMeSlY?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) or our [**FilmFreeway page**](https://us.list-manage.com/N5UfUWpEpDd?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/AeltTl6exlc?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)for more inspiration, submission details, and Atticus Award winning films from previous years!
**SAVE THE DATES:** The 6th annual, [virtual ](https://us.list-manage.com/CpXjAnn4GSs?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)[**Daddying Film Festival**](https://us.list-manage.com/bW399n84zIb?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) will take place on Eventive, **January 11-20, 2027** , and our **LIVE**[**Daddying Film Forum**](https://us.list-manage.com/QP0w_cXWFmu?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf), at American University in Washington, DC, will screen select Atticus Award winners, finalists & more **Jan 29-30, 2027**.
**The Virginia Blueprint: A Summit Advancing Men and Boys** In June, Virginia passed landmark legislation to create the nation’s first commission dedicated to boys and men. On September 18, the Virginia Coalition for Boys and Men and the Virginia Advisory Commission for Boys and Men is hosting an in-person summit that builds on that momentum – bringing together leaders from Virginia and across the country to share what works and scale proven initiatives across disciplines.
Learn more and register to get your free tickets: [https://vaboysandmen.org/ ](https://us.list-manage.com/klH7w9YQtxS?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)

| SETTING THE RECORD STRAIGHT: SENATE DEMOCRATS CLAIM CREDIT FOR GOVERNOR’S TAX CUTS Montpelier, Vt.- Senate Democrats were caught red handed this weekend, misleading Vermonters as they claimed credit for Governor Scott’s Tax Relief package from 2025. S**enator Ruth Hardy (D-Addison)** penned an op-ed lauding their effort, scolding the Governor, claiming the ideas were __“... spearheaded and crafted,” by the Democratic legislature_._ (Addison Independent 8/27/26) **Senator Joe Major (D-Windsor)** even went as far as to say in a Facebook video on Saturday, __“those tax cuts didn’t start in the executive office, they were crafted right in the legislature,”_ and _Senate Democrats “brought those savings to the negotiating table...”__ (https://www.facebook.com/reel/896746016563767) The tax cuts in question include increasing the child tax credit for kids up to the age of six, increasing the earned income tax credit, expanding the income tax exemption on social security, and excluding military pensions from the state’s income tax. **__But here’s the problem with their manufactured outrage and attempts to take credit... each of those provisions were first put forward in the Governor’s proposed FY26 budget laid out on January 28 of 2025 and highlighted in his Budget Address given before a joint session of the legislature on the same day.__** “I’m not shocked that Senate Democrats want to run from their record on taxes, but I’ve been around Montpelier a long time and I’ve never seen such blatant misrepresentation of the truth,” Dustin Degree, a former State Senator and Governor Scott’s Campaign Manager, said. Here’s an excerpt from the Governor’s Budget Address back in 2025: **_“We should provide some much-needed relief with a $13.5 million tax reduction package. Here’s what it includes:_** **_As costs have gone up, those on a fixed income are hit the hardest, so we should increase eligibility for our social security income tax exemption._** **_To help low-income working adults keep more of their paycheck, we can expand the Earned Income Tax Credit for those without dependents._** **_We can cover more families with the Child Tax Credit by extending it up to age six._** **_And as I’ve done nearly every year, I propose eliminating the income tax on military pensions – bringing us in line with nearly every other state, attracting a valuable and important part of the workforce, and making sure those who serve our nation can afford to thrive and retire here too.” _** (Journal of the Joint Assembly, 1/28/2025) Act 71, the bipartisan bill that served as a vehicle for those changes, was introduced on February 6, months after the administration began building the budget that included these measures and well after they were presented to the legislature. Claiming credit for these ideas would literally mean having a hand in drafting the Governor’s budget proposal, which these two Senators, clearly, did not. “I’m not sure what’s more difficult to believe, the fact that they would be so brazen in their attempt to claim credit for the Governor’s plan or that they think Vermonters would buy that Senate Democrats had any interest in lowering taxes on Vermonters. After all, it’s their leadership that has led to the affordability crisis that is crushing our families, farms and businesses and allowed property taxes to increase by nearly 50% in the last five years,” Degree added. After nearly thirty years of single party control in the legislature, Vermonters are feeling the full force of an agenda that has consistently raised taxes and fees while pursuing policies that make it more expensive and more difficult to live, work, do business and retire here. That’s why the Governor is focused on electing commonsense candidates from across the spectrum that are willing to work with him to provide more tax relief to Vermonters. _**You can help the Governor and mainstream candidates to deliver on a more affordable Vermont by contributing to the campaign today! **_

“One thing is clear; Democrats are worried about their record on pocketbook issues. They must be hearing what I’m hearing:_Vermonters are tapped out and looking for a new direction from the legislature_ ,” Degree said. “I guess if I were a Senate Democrat, I’d be nervous, too.”

clean_body: This is what the next two months will look like | = Peter, Summer is winding down — and at EMILYs List, that means one thing: The final sprint to Election Day is officially here. November 3 is just over two months away. Across the country, our candidates are ramping up voter outreach, getting their messages on the air, and doing everything they can to reach every last voter before polls close. And we're matching their energy — supporting Democratic pro-choice women and helping them get their messages out in the races that could decide the future of our country. = | = Here's where things stand as we head into September: 🗺️WE'VE EXPANDED OUR MAP AGAIN Last week, we announced our latest endorsement slate of five powerhouse U.S. House candidates joining our Mission Majority slate: Callie Barr (MI-01) , Trina Swanson (MN-08) , Teresa Benitez-Thompson (NV-02) , Beth Macy (VA-06) , and Carmela Conroy (WA-05). These women are making their races competitive in tougher territory because they are exactly the right candidates for their districts. They're running to flip competitive districts, put a check on MAGA Republicans' out-of-touch agenda, and fight for working families in Congress. 📈 RACES ARE SHIFTING IN OUR FAVOR There's real momentum behind EMILYs List women — and election experts are taking notice. Majority Makers like Christina Hines (MI-10) , Cait Conley (NY-17) , and Paige Cognetti (PA-08) have built strong campaigns that have helped move their races into toss-up territory. And in Texas, Gina Hinojosa (TX-GOV) is giving Greg Abbott a real fight. New Polling has shown Gina trailing Abbott by just a single point — making one thing clear: Republicans cannot take the Lone Star State for granted. 🛍️ MERCH WITH A MESSAGE Want to show your support beyond your inbox? Our latest merchandise is available in our Browse brand-new hats, shirts, pins, and more — perfect for your evening stroll, weekend canvass, or wherever else you want to make your values known. Every purchase supports our work to elect Democratic pro-choice women, so your outfit won't just make a statement. It’ll help power this movement. (And we think you'll really like what our new items have to say!) We know the closer Election Day gets, the easier it can be to feel overwhelmed by everything at stake. But this isn't the moment to tune out. It’s the moment to lean in. For the next two months, our candidates are going to give these races everything they have.
