body:
| | | | Hi Friend,
The U.S. Department of Education has designated five Northern Virginia school divisions, Alexandria City, Arlington, Fairfax, **Loudoun, and Prince William** , as high-risk grantees after finding their bathroom and locker room policies violate Title IX.
The districts have said they will keep their current policies in place, and more than $50 million in federal education funding is now tied up in reimbursement status, **with some districts headed to court.**
Here's my take: if parents had a real choice in where they sent their kids to school, our districts would have a lot more reason to drop the political antics and start focusing on a quality education instead of indoctrination.
Fights like this one drag on because families often have little to no choice in the matter.
**I believe in parental rights and school choice.**
And I believe competition is what actually fixes this, rather than a perpetual state of filing lawsuits.
**Will you chip in today and help me carry that fight to Congress?**
---
| | [CHIP IN FOR SCHOOL CHOICE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
---
| | | Parents across Northern Virginia want the same simple thing - a school that teaches their kids well and respects their family's values.
I'm asking you to stand with me so we can put that power back where it belongs, **in parents' hands** , instead of leaving it with school boards stuck in political fights.
Let's build a Congress that finally listens to Northern Virginia families.

God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

Last week, the White House made headlines with a major policy push to tackle surging grocery bills - starting with the price of beef.
President Trump signed a new executive proclamation aimed at temporarily expanding beef import quotas to bring down ground beef costs by up to 25% for American families over the next 90 days.

Naturally, the administration moved to show it's taking action.
As expected, the press spent the week running stories on the policy mechanics, trade tariffs, and immediate pushback from domestic cattle ranchers.
They're covering the policy economics, but they're missing the political strategy.
After 30 years on the front lines of political communications, I can tell you this: when it comes to grocery bills, gas prices, and rent, political perception almost always beats economic reality.
This isn't just about beef.
This is about a core rule of campaign strategy that every candidate and administration heading into election season must understand.

HELP US REACH EVERY VOTER
We have just **63 days** to get our message into every corner of PA-11 and make sure voters know they have a choice on November 3.

---

**Keeping our Ballots Accessible****** Nancy supports voting rights without constraints or deterrence. Last week, the U.S. Supreme Court cleared a legal hurdle for President Trump's effort to restrict mail-in voting. This means that people legally registered to vote risk losing access to their mail-in ballot because their name isn't on a new federal list. Congressman Lloyd Smucker has continued to support new federal voting restrictions. Will he stand up for PA-11 voters now? So far, he hasn’t. Nancy is especially concerned about seniors, members of the military, rural voters, and others who depend on voting by mail. This will affect Republicans, Democrats, and Independents. It’s also another way to tell young voters that their voice doesn’t matter – but we know it does! Voting should be secure, but it should also be accessible, and Nancy believe that everyone should register to vote and make their voice heard.****
**The Gen Z Vote Can Make a Difference in District 11!**
Across the country, about 58% of adults ages 18 to 24, part of the “Gen Z” generational cohort, said they were registered to vote in the 2024 election, according to Census Bureau data. At the same time, a 2026 study from the Civics Center found that Pennsylvania came in last among the 30 states it looked at, with just 22% of 18-year-olds registered. (Oregon topped the list at 86%, while nearby states like New Jersey were closer to 50%.)
Pennsylvania makes it more difficult for young people to register to vote by not letting most 16- and 17-year-olds pre-register and not offering same-day registration - options that many other states already have. These barriers can keep Gen Z from getting involved in politics.
Additionally, Congressman Lloyd Smucker voted against the For the People Act, a federal bill that would have made registration easier with automatic and same-day options and expanded voting access nationwide, including to the digital natives who are Gen Z. While Lloyd Smucker opposed expanding voter registration and voting options, Nancy Mannion supports making voting more accessible.
While low youth participation is a concern across the country, Pennsylvania's 11th District looks a little different. Census Bureau data shows that 69% of 18- to 24-year-olds in Lancaster and York counties were registered during the last election cycle, compared with 58% nationwide. In other words, young voters in PA-11 are ready to get involved and make their voices heard at the ballot box!
**In Pennsylvania,[teens can pre-register to vote](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsF30mRHkLv9rg1BGyPEFV/xkpIB5zgq0-n) as long as they will be 18 on election day, which this year is November 3. Teens can also [volunteer with campaigns](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFVLUdi8i151w50enNxxZ/d1rmj-BMZjnk) and canvass (the Mannion campaign sends canvassers out in pairs), phone bank, work tables at events, or suggest their own fantastic idea!**
**October 19 is the deadline to register for November’s General Election. If you know a voter who hasn’t registered yet – or maybe isn’t sure they registered – send them this[link](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFxgCq8X470CC8q2cMhfd/b3ugGzP5bIpH) to Pennsylvania’s voter registration page. You can check your own registration there, too.**
_Contributed by Riley Campbell, Gen Z, York County_

clean_body: | | | For breaking news follow us on social media | | | | | ---|--- | | | | | | | 63 DAYS TO ELECTION DAY NOVEMBER 3, 2026 ---|--- HELP US REACH EVERY VOTER We have just 63 days to get our message into every corner of PA-11 and make sure voters know they have a choice on November 3. | | Reaching voters takes resources. Billboards, digital and traditional media advertising, mail, signs, and organizing across the district all cost money. Your contribution today will help us reach more voters and build the campaign we need to win! ---|--- | Keeping our Ballots Accessible** Nancy supports voting rights without constraints or deterrence. Last week, the U.S. Supreme Court cleared a legal hurdle for President Trump's effort to restrict mail-in voting. This means that people legally registered to vote risk losing access to their mail-in ballot because their name isn't on a new federal list. Congressman Lloyd Smucker has continued to support new federal voting restrictions. Will he stand up for PA-11 voters now? So far, he hasn’t. Nancy is especially concerned about seniors, members of the military, rural voters, and others who depend on voting by mail. This will affect Republicans, Democrats, and Independents. It’s also another way to tell young voters that their voice doesn’t matter – but we know it does! Voting should be secure, but it should also be accessible, and Nancy believe that everyone should register to vote and make their voice heard. The Gen Z Vote Can Make a Difference in District 11! Across the country, about 58% of adults ages 18 to 24, part of the “Gen Z” generational cohort, said they were registered to vote in the 2024 election, according to Census Bureau data. At the same time, a 2026 study from the Civics Center found that Pennsylvania came in last among the 30 states it looked at, with just 22% of 18-year-olds registered. (Oregon topped the list at 86%, while nearby states like New Jersey were closer to 50%.) Pennsylvania makes it more difficult for young people to register to vote by not letting most 16- and 17-year-olds pre-register and not offering same-day registration - options that many other states already have. These barriers can keep Gen Z from getting involved in politics. Additionally, Congressman Lloyd Smucker voted against the For the People Act, a federal bill that would have made registration easier with automatic and same-day options and expanded voting access nationwide, including to the digital natives who are Gen Z. While Lloyd Smucker opposed expanding voter registration and voting options, Nancy Mannion supports making voting more accessible. While low youth participation is a concern across the country, Pennsylvania's 11th District looks a little different. Census Bureau data shows that 69% of 18- to 24-year-olds in Lancaster and York counties were registered during the last election cycle, compared with 58% nationwide. In other words, young voters in PA-11 are ready to get involved and make their voices heard at the ballot box! In Pennsylvania, as long as they will be 18 on election day, which this year is November 3. Teens can also and canvass (the Mannion campaign sends canvassers out in pairs), phone bank, work tables at events, or suggest their own fantastic idea! October 19 is the deadline to register for November’s General Election. If you know a voter who hasn’t registered yet – or maybe isn’t sure they registered – send them this to Pennsylvania’s voter registration page. You can check your own registration there, too. #
Peter,
We have some tough news. **We fell short of our $25,000 fundraising goal by $3,000.** Falling short right now means we’re entering a high-stakes organizing period without the full resources we urgently need to power our voter registration and mobilization efforts.
The deadline might’ve passed, but the work can’t stop. **We can still close this gap if 32 grassroots supporters from your area step up right now. Here’s how your donation of $3 or any amount can help, Peter.**
[**But if you’re ready to power our work right now, will you be one of the 32 people from your area who help us reach our goal?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20260901-1.cjTV-c&refcode=em20260901-539&t=1&akid=539%2E1366028%2EfeljWj)
**Here’s how far your $3 donation goes:**
**$3** helps power urgent voter registration efforts to fight back against the GOP’s attempts to disenfranchise people of color.
**$3** helps launch mobilization campaigns to get Latino voters to the polls in crucial battleground districts across the country where we could be the margin of victory — or defeat.
**$3** helps fund the digital outreach needed to help reach young, first-time voters feel confident and informed to vote.
**$3** helps fight back against right-wing disinformation aimed at keeping our community home.
**We only need 32 more donors from your area to reach our goal, Peter.**
**[So, with these reasons in mind, will you rush a $3 donation before midnight to help us organize in the districts that will decide control of the House and the Senate?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260901-1.7h1ftT&amount=3&refcode=em20260901-539&t=2&akid=539%2E1366028%2EfeljWj)**

Thank you,

Friend, it's Michele Tafoya, and you need to hear about what happened.

Bryce Gustafson has been knocking on doors in Indiana for more than a decade. The lead organizer with Citizens Action Coalition (CAC), a consumer and environmental organization, he usually encounters a mix of reactions when he's out canvassing--whatever issue he's talking about, there's always at least a few people on the other side. But at a recent festival in the rural town of Monrovia, Indiana, he was struck by an unusual spirit of unity.
He was there about a proposed [data center](https://substack.com/redirect/571d3819-7148-4cf4-b81c-2a30ef6953b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--a 550-acre Google project in this small town of 1,600 people. "I had 50 people I talked to," Gustafson told me. "Nobody wanted that data center in their community. And at least a half a dozen people came up to me to say, 'Hey, I voted for Trump. What the heck's he doing, supporting these things?'"
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=213574285&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjEzNTc0Mjg1LCJpYXQiOjE3ODgyODE0ODEsImV4cCI6MTc5MDg3MzQ4MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.S39uihAssjBwMvwMyz3LwSXCbRbUxqsAIZJoBrnGAXk)
Gustafson says he's had similar conversations all across the state. If there's one thing he sees uniting Hoosiers of all stripes--from rural areas like [Morgan County](https://substack.com/redirect/3b739b7c-7b31-40fd-bf4c-14f69d6b2119?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to suburbs like [Franklin Township](https://substack.com/redirect/5bd31d10-9e2d-44bc-831a-dd5de46cdc9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the historically African American neighborhood of [Martindale Brightwood](https://substack.com/redirect/c543b41a-3faa-4bd4-80ba-2a22053e338a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Indianapolis--it's fury over these water-guzzling, air-polluting behemoths and the tech oligarchs imposing them.
These dynamics are playing out across the United States. Over the last year, intensifying waves of local opposition to Big Tech's data center buildout have surged into a nationwide tsunami of resistance. Elites on both coasts, from leaders of the AI industry in Silicon Valley to leaders of the political establishment in Washington, DC, have struggled to make sense of the backlash. First they tried to write it off as business-as-usual NIMBYism: just a few local bans passed here and there, maybe some unknown city councilors [losing reelection](https://substack.com/redirect/ee7751e7-93f7-4536-a1c3-eef7f32b0d3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after signing data center deals--not such a big deal. Then Senator Bernie Sanders and Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez began calling for a national moratorium. Pretty soon [Utah's Senate President](https://substack.com/redirect/d2957a63-c755-4d68-8341-da478c157c6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) got tossed out of office for supporting hyperscale proposals. And the movement continues to grow.
Today, [three-quarters](https://substack.com/redirect/af7180c5-ab1d-4b41-9842-029f9277ce04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Americans oppose local data center development, a swing of more than 30 points in just a year. Over [500 counties and municipalities](https://substack.com/redirect/3af06498-ccbb-499d-a087-163706e0b067?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have passed data center bans or moratoria, while dozens of proposed projects have been killed outright. And the issue has come to define some of the highest-profile political races in the country. In the battle for U.S. Senate in Ohio, populist Democrat [Sherrod Brown](https://substack.com/redirect/01cd5495-ccb5-4e93-8b6d-7a90e4a9f4d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has made Republican Senator Jon Husted's support of data centers the centerpiece of his campaign, prompting [warnings](https://substack.com/redirect/bbdf57f7-799f-4c63-96a9-997f6e82c55f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the National Republican Senatorial Committee that "data centers are the anchor hanging around Husted's neck."
Other Republicans are taking notice. Texas Governor Greg Abbot once touted the state as the "epicenter of AI development"; last week he said data centers had "dug their own grave." In Michigan, days after The Lever [revealed](https://substack.com/redirect/b2cd10b8-4fd1-49f1-a208-617138817b20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers held millions in AI-related investments, he announced his support for a one-year moratorium on their construction in the state.
Big Tech billionaires may finally be [beginning](https://substack.com/redirect/4d7f4d92-fd4b-40e0-a44f-a32f7f466681?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to realize that this backlash poses real complications for them. But they still [don't understand](https://substack.com/redirect/e7ffd1f2-7852-4673-bbc7-7257bef21d36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the nature of the threat they've called down upon themselves. Because the movement against data centers represents more than just a series of local fights against a new kind of infrastructure project. It may, in fact, constitute the best opportunity we've had in generations to truly shake up American politics--by redirecting the partisan anger that oligarchic forces have long used to divide regular Americans and channeling that energy instead against the billionaires that are actually the cause of so many of our shared problems.
The political science term for this strategy, coined by [Jennifer McCoy and Murat Somer](https://substack.com/redirect/e2d72279-57c3-4dd3-9698-ac35e886833f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), is "transformative repolarization." McCoy and Somer argue that authoritarians and oligarchs often stoke what they call "pernicious polarization"--extreme toxic polarization that uses "us versus them" rhetoric, often on social and culture war issues, to divide the public in ways that harm democracy. In the face of such intense suspicion and distrust, depolarizing a society--trying to get people to stop viewing their fellow citizens as an existential danger--may not work on its own, in the absence of a unifying struggle to address underlying grievances. Instead, McCoy and Somer argue that opponents of authoritarianism need to redraw the lines of contestation that define their politics--to shift the "us versus them" struggle from, for example, a left-to-right polarization, to a different axis of conflict that can bring a large majority of the public together against real structural threats.
When you speak to organizers and community leaders on the front lines of local data center campaigns, it immediately becomes clear that they are seeing new configurations of people coming together in precisely this way. "On many issues, people come in with a baked-in partisan lens that influences their thinking," said Ben Inskeep, program director at CAC. "On data centers, we don't have those firm camps formed. And so we're seeing broad concern from Republicans, Democrats, and everyone else on the political spectrum. We're seeing folks saying, hey, I might be a MAGA Republican and you might be a liberal yahoo from the big city, but if you're coming to our community to help us fight this data center, you're my best friend."
William Lawrence has been seeing the same thing in Michigan. The Sunrise Movement co-founder and congressional candidate made opposition to data centers a major focus of his successful campaign for the Democratic nomination to represent the Lansing area. He's now hammering his Republican opponent on the issue--to great apparent effect, according to a [recent poll](https://substack.com/redirect/01254f16-3540-4419-8fd9-d61c0a4a280e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) finding Lawrence leading in the district, which is currently held by a Republican. "At a time when people are so polarized and isolated from each other, something that brings people together is rare," he said. "We can all get together to watch the Spartans play at Spartan Stadium, but to get together in a context where you're also talking about politics? That is a gift, and is not at all to be taken for granted."
An organizer I spoke with who's been opposing data center construction in Texas (who asked to remain anonymous) noted a similar dynamic playing out in his state. "I've never seen anything that mobilizes this many rural Texans before," he told me. "Folks are starting to get politicized through this work. They're realizing when they reach out to their state reps, their state senators, that these people are not batting for them. They're batting for the tech oligarchs. And so people are realizing that the left-to-right divide isn't as important as the divide between the working class and the big corporate interests."
The electoral implications of this process should be obvious. But for anyone too thick to draw their own conclusions, voters themselves are starting to get quite explicit. When MS Now asked a woman in 80-percent-Republican Hood County, Texas, "You're willing to forgo every conservative issue and let the Senate fall into the hands of Democrats if that's what it takes to kill data centers?" her [response](https://substack.com/redirect/48388cc1-f5f8-4b9c-8c00-636665f1ed15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was immediate: "Yep. My entire community's going to break rank."
What remains to be seen is whether Democrats will seize this massive opportunity--or let Republicans regain the initiative.
### A Manifestation of Greed
"I've been waiting a long time for people to wake up to how they're being ripped off," Gustafson told me. So why are data centers the issue that's finally waking people up?
For one, they're essentially unique in the breadth of their odiousness--so everyone has a reason to be offended by them. Hyperscale data centers are massive industrial warehouses that can cover literally dozens of acres, generate debilitating noise pollution, and severely impact [local water ](https://substack.com/redirect/504bd10e-b9fb-4fad-a197-f1eace0cc72e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)tables. They use [obscene](https://substack.com/redirect/918a989f-101d-4857-86da-a7245b34f816?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) amounts of energy, [straining](https://substack.com/redirect/fbc01722-4af4-4697-842b-16342ff68973?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) local infrastructure and in many cases causing utility rates to spike. This also has devastating climate and environmental impacts, as AI developers are overwhelmingly meeting their energy needs with dirty fossil fuel generators that spew outrageous amounts of [planet-warming emissions](https://substack.com/redirect/8e1474b0-0717-4eb8-9e3a-619e55b94be6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and severely impact local air quality.
Then there are the process concerns: use of [eminent domain](https://substack.com/redirect/cd665a04-3e52-418c-870a-ea413784612d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the provision of [taxpayer subsidies](https://substack.com/redirect/c1b5ed0f-e63a-4f32-bd34-71fbf082c7fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and Big Tech's near-ubiquitous practice of pushing local officials to sign [non-disclosure agreements](https://substack.com/redirect/2dc92801-f6c8-4b67-8141-6b8866c1d28c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (NDAs) that shroud deals in suspicious opacity.
And all of this is for what? Though the development of data centers creates temporary construction work, once developed, the facilities do not provide communities with significant long-term jobs. The only thing these sites produce (other than many shades of pollution) is added compute for a technology that we've all been told will soon put billions of people out of work. In the meantime, as we wait to see whether that dystopian future materializes or it was all an economy-wrecking [bubble](https://substack.com/redirect/9cba5297-5e20-4334-aeb4-e64d539e6000?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), AI is largely being experienced as the thing making the internet more annoying, our jobs more stressful, surveillance more terrifying, and Big Tech billionaires--already widely despised--more powerful than ever. It's not hard to understand why this doesn't constitute a very compelling case for data centers.
What it does provide is a perfect canvas on which to illustrate the broader problems with our political and economic system--how a few individuals have all the money and power to control the decisions that impact our lives. "Data centers are the physical manifestation of the greed and the hubris and the power of the AI oligarchs," Gustafson said. "That gets people thinking about why we are allowing these tech billionaires to just run roughshod over our state."
What emerges from this process is a budding sense of solidarity that can extend far beyond the localized concerns that might have brought someone into a particular fight. Gustafson described how organizers from Evansville, a city in southwest Indiana, began supporting groups across the border in Kentucky when fights started ratcheting up there. Elsewhere, a farmer who became the leader of a data center fight in Henry County, Indiana, attended a meeting about a proposed project in a neighboring town. "Next thing you know, she's helping that community, showing up for them, because it's so much easier getting through this when you have somebody who's been there and understands," he said.
As Inskeep put it: "When one campaign ends, people are saying, 'Hey, we fought ours, now that it's done, we're going to go to the next county and help them.'" And that starts a snowball effect. "People are seeing that they're stronger together. It's a beautiful thing."
### A Singular Opportunity
Clearly, these fights have created an opening for the left. But the politics around data centers are still very much up for grabs. Democrats should have a strong inherent edge, given that--on this issue, like so many others--President Donald Trump has forcefully aligned himself with his buddies in the billionaire class. Trump's [aggressive plans](https://substack.com/redirect/345bfacd-c12a-4b5a-ade3-c7e2b903a9cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to accelerate Big Tech's data center buildout include opening up federal lands for hyperscaler construction, axing public participation processes in permitting, and even [waiving](https://substack.com/redirect/bef934f8-1ca1-493e-9e0d-182b0d8d55c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act requirements on the radically absurd grounds that data center approvals need to be expedited for [national security](https://substack.com/redirect/4908af85-6043-47ae-880e-974b84f1e243?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reasons.
But other conservative forces have been ahead of the curve. Steve Bannon has long been [working](https://substack.com/redirect/31ce6bde-54fe-4363-99b1-b2fe3b13e267?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to put MAGA's populist wing out front in opposing both data centers and AI more broadly. The Texas organizer I spoke with told me he sees a significant number of people coming into data center fights casting blame not on Big Tech oligarchs, but on China or the United Arab Emirates, in ways that can feel decidedly xenophobic or Islamophobic. "This is an opportunity, but it's a short-lived opportunity and we need to seize it," said Inskeep. "Because this can also be used against us. If we are not effective at doing the political education and helping folks through that process, I do think you could have a far-right, nationalist, anti-immigrant person use this issue to come to power and then implement horrifying policies."
Needless to say, for Democrats to seize this opportunity, they first must actually take a unified stance against data centers. And unfortunately, many Democratic leaders remain just as in-bed with Big Tech billionaires as their GOP counterparts. Maine's Democratic governor Janet Mills [vetoed](https://substack.com/redirect/c3e17bac-aac5-4c3e-a762-7f494fb233dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the data center moratorium passed by her state legislature. Michigan's Democratic governor Gretchen Whitmer was [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/2d9d1af8-8299-498d-a2a8-6fcfba37c964?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of dismissing her constituents' concerns about the many data center projects she has supported. Democratic Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries [opposes](https://substack.com/redirect/283864e6-d776-4008-9739-079df7fe7609?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a data center moratorium and [appointed](https://substack.com/redirect/595763cb-7f2a-48ef-a171-cbcc6988a4e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the aggressively corporatist Josh Gottheimer and Big Tech-backed Zoe Lofgren to help develop House Democrats' AI platform.
And there are some races where Democrats are squarely on the losing side of the issue. In Wisconsin, the Democratic nominee for governor, David Crowley, is already being [blasted in ads](https://substack.com/redirect/561b537d-259b-4a11-8c1b-509c7599e84c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by his Republican opponent for having said he wants Wisconsin to "become an AI and a data hub not only for the entire country, but for the entire globe." Crowley won his gubernatorial primary after the entire Democratic establishment united to oppose the left-leaning candidate in the race, Francesca Hong, on the grounds that old "woke" posts--most famously a call to "cancel Thanksgiving"--made her [unelectable](https://substack.com/redirect/1b427f64-653d-44ec-9fc7-7a5b86d1d542?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But Crowley's troubles demonstrate why Democrats need to update their assumptions regarding what kinds of past statements make for real electoral liabilities. After all, nobody is actually going to cancel Thanksgiving. But making Wisconsin into a hub of hated data centers? That feels like a very real possibility to a lot of Wisconsin's swing voters.
When I asked Lawrence what he'd want to say to party leadership on this point, his response was simple. "I would say, listen to the people. Nobody wants companies from Silicon Valley coming in, bullying us, making decisions that are going to impact the next century of our communities. Just listen to the people. You'll be popular."
So will Democrats take the chance they've been given? For the first time in generations, the billionaire class has overreached in a way that Americans of all stripes and ideologies are finding equally repulsive. They've created a perfect opening to repolarize the public--not just against Trump, but against the oligarchic and authoritarian systems that produced him in the first place.
The opportunity before us is singular. What a monstrous mistake it would be not to seize it.

# Join Documenting Hope at the Health & Healing Expo
---
|
---
| We are excited to support our friends at **Documenting Hope** for their upcoming **Health & Healing Expo, November 21–22, 2026, in Orlando, Florida**. Explore the future of root cause healing at the intersection of cutting edge science and practical solutions for families. This immersive event will bring together leading experts, innovative technologies, and actionable strategies covering the microbiome, mitochondria, metabolism, nervous system regulation, therapeutic diets, photobiomodulation, fascial healing, environmental health, and inspiring real world healing stories. **Good news for the Autism Health community!** Documenting Hope has extended its Conference Flash Sale exclusively for members of the **Autism Health community**. Purchase your ticket **before September 11th** and receive **FREE access to the complete video library from the 2024 Conference, a $199 value!** This is a wonderful opportunity to attend the upcoming event while gaining access to hours of additional educational content. After purchasing your ticket, simply email **info@documentinghope.com** and let their team know you purchased your ticket and heard about the free offer through **Autism Health**. They will send you a coupon to access the 2024 Conference videos at no cost. **Don't miss this special offer and the opportunity to connect, learn, and explore new possibilities for whole person health and healing!**
---

# Join Us for Our September Autism Support Group
---
|
---
| We invite you to join us for our next **Autism Support Group** on **Tuesday, September 8th at 4:00 PM PST / 7:00 PM EST** via Zoom. Whether you are a parent, caregiver, family member, self advocate, or professional, this monthly gathering provides a welcoming and supportive space to connect with others who understand the autism journey. Our support group is an opportunity to share experiences, ask questions, exchange resources, celebrate victories, and receive encouragement from a compassionate community. Together, we learn from one another, discuss challenges and solutions, and build meaningful relationships that remind us we are never alone. At Autism Health, we believe that connection is one of the most powerful tools for healing and hope. No matter where you are on your journey, you are welcome to join us. **Advance registration through Zoom is required to attend.** Please register using the link below to receive your Zoom access information. We look forward to seeing you on **Tuesday, September 8th at 4:00 PM PST!**
---
| [REGISTER HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/5h8cqVj3Mdq?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "REGISTER HERE")

# Early Bird Registration for the Autism Health Summit
---
|
---
| The countdown has begun for the **2027 Autism Health Summit** , taking place **April 29 through May 1, 2027** , at **The Legacy Center Resort & Spa** in **San Diego, California**. Join parents, physicians, researchers, healthcare professionals, educators, and advocates from around the world for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and hope. We're excited to announce that our **headline speakers** include **Del Bigtree** , **Dr. Henry Ealy, and Tyler Hudson** , with many more nationally recognized experts to be announced in the coming months. Attendees will gain valuable insights into the latest research, innovative therapies, integrative medicine, environmental health, and practical strategies to support individuals with autism and related neurological conditions. We're also pleased to offer **Continuing Medical Education (CME)** and **Continuing Education Unit (CEU)** credits for eligible healthcare professionals, making the Autism Health Summit an outstanding opportunity to expand your knowledge while earning valuable continuing education credits. **Now is the best time to register!** Secure your ticket before prices increase and receive **$50 OFF** your registration during the month of **September** by using promo code **AHS50** at checkout. This special offer expires at the end of the month. Whether you're a parent, caregiver, practitioner, educator, therapist, or advocate, the Autism Health Summit offers an unparalleled opportunity to learn from leading experts, connect with a passionate community, and leave empowered with practical knowledge you can apply immediately. **Reserve your seat today using the registration link below. We look forward to welcoming you to San Diego, April 29 through May 1, 2027!**
---

# Join Us for Our Winter Gala!
---
|
---
| **Join Us for an Unforgettable Evening at the Autism Health Winter Gala** We are thrilled to invite you to the **First Annual Autism Health Winter Gala** , taking place on **Saturday, January 30, 2027** , at the beautiful **Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida**. This elegant evening will bring together supporters, physicians, researchers, community leaders, and families for a memorable celebration. Guests will enjoy an inspiring evening featuring a VIP reception, dinner, exciting live and silent auctions, and presentations from nationally recognized leaders. We are honored to announce **General Michael Flynn** and **Del Bigtree **as our featured speakers. We have also extended an invitation to **Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.** , whose participation will be confirmed at a later date. The Winter Gala is more than a celebration. It is an opportunity to invest in the future of Autism Health. Proceeds from this special event will directly support our mission to provide educational webinars, parent support groups, scholarships for families, research initiatives, conferences, and community programs that improve the lives of individuals with autism and related neurological conditions. For a limited time only, you can receive **10% off** your admission ticket with promo code **Gala10**. Whether you are a longtime supporter or are just learning about Autism Health, we invite you to join us for an evening of inspiration, generosity, and meaningful connection. Together, we can continue expanding access to education, advancing research, and providing hope to families across the country. **Reserve your seat today using the registration link below. We look forward to celebrating with you in Jupiter, Florida!**

* * *
Yesterday, Donald Trump's Supreme Court told him he could keep building his stupid taxpayer-funded ballroom.
I wasn't surprised. You shouldn't be either. But the ballroom isn't really the story. It's just the latest blip. At this point, the operating assumption should be that this Court will let this man do essentially anything he wants, and the only real question is how they'll dress it up on the way to saying yes. That is not a court. That is a permission slip. It is a partisan institution staffed with political operatives who are not interested in acting as jurists, not interested in the rule of law, and not interested in the American people. They are interested in outcomes. They have been for a long time.
That building has been corrupted -- by Trump, by the absentee Mitch McConnell, and by a few decades' worth of Republicans who figured out that if you can't win the argument, you buy the referee. There is no integrity left in it. And I want to be careful here, because I know how that sounds. I'm not saying it to be edgy. I'm saying it because my entire adult political life has been shaped by that Court making decisions that a rational person cannot square with anything resembling law.
I am still mad about Bush v. Gore. Genuinely, in my chest, still mad. I believe Al Gore would have been president if they had simply let people finish counting the votes. That's it. That's the whole ask. Count the votes. The Supreme Court of the United States stopped the counting of votes in an American election, and most people went to brunch. Then 9/11 happened and we all forgot.
Then watch what McConnell did. He held a Supreme Court seat hostage for a year to keep Barack Obama from filling it. Then, when the Access Hollywood tape dropped and Donald Trump's political career was lying on the floor of the Republican Party bleeding out, that stolen seat is what resuscitated him. It gave every squeamish Republican a reason to hold their nose and get in line. McConnell didn't just steal a seat from Obama. He saved Trump. And then the rules kept changing, and the arguments kept getting more transparently full of shit, and the political press kept nodding along like they were covering a tennis match instead of a heist. McConnell understood something Democrats have spent far too long refusing to understand: power unused is power surrendered. He had it. He used it. And we have been living with the consequences ever since.
And here we are. A Court that has decided the president is essentially immune for his crimes. A Court where four justices were unwilling to fully say that a president cannot rewrite the Constitution with the stroke of an executive order. A Court that gives this man whatever he asks for. And an administration that keeps coming back, keeps pushing, keeps testing every remaining guardrail -- birthright citizenship, mail-in ballots, executive power, whatever comes next. And you can bet your last dollar that the second we elect a Democratic president, these same people will rediscover their deep and abiding concern about the limits of executive power -- right on time, right when we need that power to actually do something for somebody.
So let me say the thing plainly. Democrats are never going to deliver the kind of lasting change this country needs until we are willing to confront what has happened to this Court -- and what it represents. Not "message better." Not "win the news cycle." Reset the Court. Undo what Trump and McConnell did to what is supposed to be the most important check in this entire system. And stop pretending that preserving broken institutions is the same thing as defending them.
That means hard decisions -- exactly the kind of decisions that technocratic, credentialed, deeply cautious Democrats have spent my whole career avoiding. We may need to add seats. We absolutely need serious ethics reform, because there are multiple justices who are very obviously taking bribes, who have relationships they will not disclose, who refuse to recuse when their friends and benefactors have business in front of them. I have come around to term limits. And I want radical financial transparency -- not just for the Court, but for every politician in this country. Health records too. We are being lied to, and we have been lied to by multiple generations of politicians, and yes, the members of the Supreme Court are politicians whether they'll admit it or not.
This requires wholesale reform. And it requires a Democratic Party willing to actually do it.
* * *

If you want to help build a politics that moves with urgency for working people instead of billionaires and demagogues, become a paid subscriber. $8/month keeps this work going and helps us reach more people.](https://substack.com/redirect/f1e4c623-4083-49f5-bd5a-f919a979f36c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

_Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know._
* * *
And that reform can't stop at the Court. The immunity ruling may make criminal prosecution extraordinarily difficult, but civil liability still matters. Following money made through bribery, extortion, insider trading, or market manipulation matters. Other countries have done this after corrupt regimes -- Peru after Fujimori, the Philippines after Marcos, Nigeria after Abacha -- recovering billions through permanent investigative institutions and international cooperation.
We _must_ be prepared to do the same. Because if the Trump family walks away from this era vastly wealthier than it entered it, that money becomes power -- and power becomes protection. We're handing the next generation the money and influence to make sure they're even harder to hold accountable than the last.
I have been a loyal Democrat my entire life. I intend to be one for as long as I have air in my lungs, as long as this party is fighting for working people and for our individual freedoms. But I'll tell you where my line is. When we take back the House, and we take back the Senate, and we take back the White House -- if this party doesn't take the steps necessary to make sure that what we've lived through in the last year and a half can never happen again, if we go right back to protecting norms that Republicans already destroyed, I will be standing right alongside most of you trying to burn the whole damn thing down.
Because Republicans did this. Let's be clear about that. But part of the reason we're here is that Democrats wouldn't do the hard thing when it was available to us. We could have banned insider trading. We could have fixed the Court. We could have fixed campaign finance. We didn't. And the why matters: it's an adherence to norms that don't actually exist anymore, a Washington culture that protects its own, and a bone-deep unwillingness to stand up to entrenched power and concentrated wealth. It's a fear of using power because somebody might accuse us of using power. Meanwhile, Republicans use it. Relentlessly.
That has to stop, and I think it's starting to. In my conversations with clients, with candidates thinking about running, with organizers and staffers -- more people understand this now than at any point in my career. What Trump has done over the last eighteen months has radicalized people inside our own party into realizing that our relationship to power is broken. We have spent too much time treating power like something dirty instead of what it actually is: a tool. The question isn't whether you use it. The question is what you use it for.
We should emulate his urgency. But only his urgency. Nothing else. He wakes up every day and moves with total speed to lie and cheat and steal from the American people. He doesn't wonder whether he's moving too fast. He doesn't worry whether some fucking panel on cable news will call him too aggressive. He identifies the power available to him and uses every inch of it. That's why I named this thing Endless Urgency -- it's my personal motto, but it's also what I watched him do, and what I want us to do in reverse. Move that fast so people don't go bankrupt when they get sick. Move that fast so forty hours of work buys a decent life. Move that fast so people can live with dignity and self-determination. Move that fast to repair the institutions they've broken. Move that fast to give people a government they can actually believe in again.
We have done it before. We're the party of the New Deal. We're the party of the Great Society. We're the party that carried the Civil Rights Act across the finish line. Goddamn it, remember who we are.
So when you feel that rage watching this Court do the inevitable -- hand this man more power -- don't let it curdle. The Republican Party lost its way by becoming a party of grievance, punishing enemies because it feels good. We don't do that. We take the rage and we turn it into action, and we wield power for the vast majority of Americans who already agree with us on the issues but have stopped believing we can deliver. Their rage became cruelty. We don't do that. Ours has to become construction. We take the rage and we turn it into action, and we wield power for the vast majority of Americans who already ag ree with us on the issues but have stopped believing we can deliver. And then we fucking deliver.
We can be that party again. I believe it.
Let's get to work.
With urgency,
--Mike

I wasn't surprised. You shouldn't be either. But the ballroom isn't really the story. It's just the latest blip. At this point, the operating assumption should be that this Court will let this man do essentially anything he wants, and the only real question is how they'll dress it up on the way to saying yes. That is not a court. That is a permission slip. It is a partisan institution staffed with political operatives who are not interested in acting as jurists, not interested in the rule of law, and not interested in the American people. They are interested in outcomes. They have been for a long time. That building has been corrupted -- by Trump, by the absentee Mitch McConnell, and by a few decades' worth of Republicans who figured out that if you can't win the argument, you buy the referee. There is no integrity left in it. And I want to be careful here, because I know how that sounds. I'm not saying it to be edgy. I'm saying it because my entire adult political life has been shaped by that Court making decisions that a rational person cannot square with anything resembling law. I am still mad about Bush v. Gore. Genuinely, in my chest, still mad. I believe Al Gore would have been president if they had simply let people finish counting the votes. That's it. That's the whole ask. Count the votes. The Supreme Court of the United States stopped the counting of votes in an American election, and most people went to brunch. Then 9/11 happened and we all forgot. Then watch what McConnell did. He held a Supreme Court seat hostage for a year to keep Barack Obama from filling it. Then, when the Access Hollywood tape dropped and Donald Trump's political career was lying on the floor of the Republican Party bleeding out, that stolen seat is what resuscitated him. It gave every squeamish Republican a reason to hold their nose and get in line. McConnell didn't just steal a seat from Obama. He saved Trump. And then the rules kept changing, and the arguments kept getting more transparently full of shit, and the political press kept nodding along like they were covering a tennis match instead of a heist. McConnell understood something Democrats have spent far too long refusing to understand: power unused is power surrendered. He had it. He used it. And we have been living with the consequences ever since. And here we are. A Court that has decided the president is essentially immune for his crimes. A Court where four justices were unwilling to fully say that a president cannot rewrite the Constitution with the stroke of an executive order. A Court that gives this man whatever he asks for. And an administration that keeps coming back, keeps pushing, keeps testing every remaining guardrail -- birthright citizenship, mail-in ballots, executive power, whatever comes next. And you can bet your last dollar that the second we elect a Democratic president, these same people will rediscover their deep and abiding concern about the limits of executive power -- right on time, right when we need that power to actually do something for somebody. So let me say the thing plainly. Democrats are never going to deliver the kind of lasting change this country needs until we are willing to confront what has happened to this Court -- and what it represents. Not "message better." Not "win the news cycle." Reset the Court. Undo what Trump and McConnell did to what is supposed to be the most important check in this entire system. And stop pretending that preserving broken institutions is the same thing as defending them. That means hard decisions -- exactly the kind of decisions that technocratic, credentialed, deeply cautious Democrats have spent my whole career avoiding. We may need to add seats. We absolutely need serious ethics reform, because there are multiple justices who are very obviously taking bribes, who have relationships they will not disclose, who refuse to recuse when their friends and benefactors have business in front of them. I have come around to term limits. And I want radical financial transparency -- not just for the Court, but for every politician in this country. Health records too. We are being lied to, and we have been lied to by multiple generations of politicians, and yes, the members of the Supreme Court are politicians whether they'll admit it or not. This requires wholesale reform. And it requires a Democratic Party willing to actually do it. Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know. * And that reform can't stop at the Court. The immunity ruling may make criminal prosecution extraordinarily difficult, but civil liability still matters. Following money made through bribery, extortion, insider trading, or market manipulation matters. Other countries have done this after corrupt regimes -- Peru after Fujimori, the Philippines after Marcos, Nigeria after Abacha -- recovering billions through permanent investigative institutions and international cooperation. We must be prepared to do the same. Because if the Trump family walks away from this era vastly wealthier than it entered it, that money becomes power -- and power becomes protection. We're handing the next generation the money and influence to make sure they're even harder to hold accountable than the last. I have been a loyal Democrat my entire life. I intend to be one for as long as I have air in my lungs, as long as this party is fighting for working people and for our individual freedoms. But I'll tell you where my line is. When we take back the House, and we take back the Senate, and we take back the White House -- if this party doesn't take the steps necessary to make sure that what we've lived through in the last year and a half can never happen again, if we go right back to protecting norms that Republicans already destroyed, I will be standing right alongside most of you trying to burn the whole damn thing down. Because Republicans did this. Let's be clear about that. But part of the reason we're here is that Democrats wouldn't do the hard thing when it was available to us. We could have banned insider trading. We could have fixed the Court. We could have fixed campaign finance. We didn't. And the why matters: it's an adherence to norms that don't actually exist anymore, a Washington culture that protects its own, and a bone-deep unwillingness to stand up to entrenched power and concentrated wealth. It's a fear of using power because somebody might accuse us of using power. Meanwhile, Republicans use it. Relentlessly. That has to stop, and I think it's starting to. In my conversations with clients, with candidates thinking about running, with organizers and staffers -- more people understand this now than at any point in my career. What Trump has done over the last eighteen months has radicalized people inside our own party into realizing that our relationship to power is broken. We have spent too much time treating power like something dirty instead of what it actually is: a tool. The question isn't whether you use it. The question is what you use it for. We should emulate his urgency. But only his urgency. Nothing else. He wakes up every day and moves with total speed to lie and cheat and steal from the American people. He doesn't wonder whether he's moving too fast. He doesn't worry whether some fucking panel on cable news will call him too aggressive. He identifies the power available to him and uses every inch of it. That's why I named this thing Endless Urgency -- it's my personal motto, but it's also what I watched him do, and what I want us to do in reverse. Move that fast so people don't go bankrupt when they get sick. Move that fast so forty hours of work buys a decent life. Move that fast so people can live with dignity and self-determination. Move that fast to repair the institutions they've broken. Move that fast to give people a government they can actually believe in again. We have done it before. We're the party of the New Deal. We're the party of the Great Society. We're the party that carried the Civil Rights Act across the finish line. Goddamn it, remember who we are. So when you feel that rage watching this Court do the inevitable -- hand this man more power -- don't let it curdle. The Republican Party lost its way by becoming a party of grievance, punishing enemies because it feels good. We don't do that. We take the rage and we turn it into action, and we wield power for the vast majority of Americans who already agree with us on the issues but have stopped believing we can deliver. Their rage became cruelty. We don't do that. Ours has to become construction. We take the rage and we turn it into action, and we wield power for the vast majority of Americans who already ag ree with us on the issues but have stopped believing we can deliver. And then we fucking deliver. We can be that party again. I believe it. Let's get to work. With urgency, --Mike Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. # [Japan's 10-year just hit 3% for the first time since '96, The cheap-money era is officially dead](https://substack.com/redirect/bf52ffb4-cbba-4f78-96a4-b3ac13759b7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Global **[bond yields jumped Tuesday as Japan's 10-year reached 3%](https://substack.com/redirect/70f5e979-3299-43db-ad41-c1ca82970a66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for the first time since 1996, U.K. gilts hit 5.23%, and the U.S. 10-year rose to 4.788%, a 20-month high.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bf52ffb4-cbba-4f78-96a4-b3ac13759b7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Britain and Europe join:** U.K. 10-year gilts reached 5.23%, the highest since June 2008, while Germany's 10-year bund yielded 3.35% and France's 10-year reached 4.21%.
* **Yen slips past 160:** The yen traded around 160.1 per dollar as Bessent said he expects Tokyo and the Bank of Japan to act, after talks with Katayama and Ueda on fiscal policy and rate hikes.
* **Crowding-out replaces war:** Bloomberg's global sovereign yield gauge hit 3.72%, the highest since mid-2008, as the selloff shifted from a war premium toward crowding-out.
* **Oil keeps inflation alive:** Brent sat above $92 and WTI above $87 after Hormuz tanker strikes, while Kudlow argued the long-bond climb is stronger growth, not a jump in inflation expectations.

# [Pentagon locks 7-year deals to triple Patriots and 4x THAAD](https://substack.com/redirect/bf52ffb4-cbba-4f78-96a4-b3ac13759b7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Department of War **[signed 7-year multiyear procurement pacts](https://substack.com/redirect/85df955f-90a7-46f1-9f4c-71a8ff13eb67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with General Dynamics and Lockheed Martin to accelerate THAAD and PAC-3 MSE interceptor output after air-defense stocks were drawn down.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bf52ffb4-cbba-4f78-96a4-b3ac13759b7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Minimum buys unlock factories:** The frameworks guarantee minimum annual quantities so General Dynamics and lower-tier suppliers can invest in workers, bulk materials, and plant upgrades.
* **Duffey cites Arsenal of Freedom:** Under Secretary Michael P. Duffey said the deals expand the "Arsenal of Freedom," cut red tape, and scale domestic manufacturing so the warfighter "never faces a fair fight."
* **Iran war drained magazines:** Unconfirmed estimates say as much as 80% of the Army's inventory of these interceptors was expended, mostly against Iranian ballistic missiles.
* **China risk sets the pace:** The article argues a near-peer fight would burn interceptors faster than the Iran campaign, making live assembly lines a strategic necessity.

* **No relief until Ukraine ends:** Bessent held a bilateral with Siluanov and cut off talk of cooperation, saying there would be no economic relief for Moscow while the Ukraine war continues.
* **Klingbeil calls it troubling:** German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said receiving the Russian minister "sends a troubling signal" and that he would not pose for a photo with him.
* **Poland says do not trust:** Polish Finance Minister Andrzej Domanski said Russia lies "constantly" and that any conversation with Moscow would be "very difficult."
* **Deregulation is the pitch:** Bessent told the G20 to "get back to the basics," citing a 129-to-1 U.S. rule-cut ratio and blaming red tape, bad taxes, and weak investment for slow global growth.

* * *
* * *
# [China dribbled out 28 tons. The U.S. slammed the scrap door](https://substack.com/redirect/bf52ffb4-cbba-4f78-96a4-b3ac13759b7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The **[United States halted tungsten scrap exports](https://substack.com/redirect/83bd3731-c944-475c-ac41-3d71f33b0f95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as China licensed only 28 tons of APT in the first half of 2026, tightening supply of a metal the West uses in munitions, drills, and chips.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bf52ffb4-cbba-4f78-96a4-b3ac13759b7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Scrap now stays home:** A U.S. tungsten-scrap export ban is live, requiring licenses and keeping 100% of scrap domestic for at least the next year to block sales to China.
* **China 's faucet is a trickle:** Restrictive licenses in place since February 2025 held Chinese APT exports to 28 tons in the first half, versus China's historic grip of about 80% of world supply.
* **Sangdong is the West 's bet:** Almonty's Sangdong mine is billed as about 40% of Western tungsten output once it reaches full capacity.
* **Price already went eightfold:** APT prices were cited around $3,000 per metric ton unit, after an eightfold jump in a little more than a year.

Fellow Patriot - I'm going to be straight with you, because that's the only way I know how to do this.

_We just won._ Two elections in two weeks: the special primary, then the runoff.

Grueling doesn't begin to cover it. Every dollar this campaign had went into turning out voters, running ads, and getting our message into every corner of this state.

**And it worked.**

But here's the part nobody tells you on election night: winning a runoff doesn't put a single dollar back in our account. Right now, after everything we just spent, our campaign finances are running on fumes.

**Annie Andrews has $4.1 million.**

She's raised nearly $11 million since she got into this race, from liberal donors across the country. She's had months to build that war chest while we were fighting a two-round primary just to get our name on the November ballot.

Countless conservatives in SC put their trust in me, and I promise to carry forward the conservative agenda for the next six years in the United States Senate. After asking me to run, President Trump stood on stage with me and told you why he trusts me, too. I don't intend to let a bigger bank account decide whether I get to keep that promise.

**[But I need you with me, starting today.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=de2b80aba4a54adf9336c2fcbcbe921c&_e=YbSyDLciqsNGY3ktMUO4y0zSwTCrfo0Uyvk_5IgupVO7xwFjRok0sJaxuwwqdH0k0dB-dCfuDxjsmAIeNut78wKdMGLqzT6JuGpJ-HiboUn5mK2a0pk4Xy34Yn6iTFrwpq234FfkUvoD4D3hB8-bJaSgUaR-UUuGvY5ySnLXd_PpPCtLwlOOwu5_0IBa81i5GfzXTWo-T9Rt0-rvK6luToeIXhCw3_sGxY4N2PkBWf-2G1xSgscxhanKKju8nDVbA0_slvYWiaN0IM6vS7ODIBIjQGHCldlyAENFkCSQAuHFFObpDZVYCvlqkUBwvFebdhYVUFvRP6-cV25whvrlV4Uf0eFgZNWr-AdIUdB7xTIjEfMv2OWhJKvq6F7s9hH3Oircxntrp_pNjW32WN36t7BrjwXb9rfxq1AoWSUb6tbYmskGZUygL27TD5iaDuWW_1VQqvuqNgQ15iiWcz_K0jW2hVmbLIfJyQwtTmdxCJlqQx8iqhl_I7mVWnmAWPv94W1mCdefinLTJEZLxaLA6cFq-RMNMjn_2hOQ2IT86nkLm2vD1_Rxk2al92L6FyI-TL3uhxkWnjgUj_-KbBracq0bNmSEEjKS4f1TxOTmpKTEG8qi_QG1y1BOCwNG2mN2XH1ggHlvL3pAf_8MuKFF4492KayPE9-RTJc5fR4tBPoP9_CF8vsB_PorNnpF7c7MPBUcqLrOz5QlUMkPLnyVeAP4wzxrPnOToJXwABY_DAHVtZlIgQY9Z913k3XLcWvm)**

November is less than 70 days away. | Fellow Patriot - I'm going to be straight with you, because that's the only way I know how to do this. We just won. Two elections in two weeks: the special primary, then the runoff. Grueling doesn't begin to cover it. But here's the part nobody tells you on election night: winning a runoff doesn't put a single dollar back in our account. Right now, after everything we just spent, our campaign finances are running on fumes. Annie Andrews has $4.1 million. She's raised nearly $11 million since she got into this race, from liberal donors across the country. She's had months to build that war chest while we were fighting a two-round primary just to get our name on the November ballot. Countless conservatives in SC put their trust in me, and I promise to carry forward the conservative agenda for the next six years in the United States Senate. After asking me to run, President Trump stood on stage with me and told you why he trusts me, too. I don't intend to let a bigger bank account decide whether I get to keep that promise. **With exactly 9 weeks until the general election, I know we can still make up lost ground if we act now.**

clean_body: I know we can close the gap if enough folks like you take action today. I’ll be honest with you, Peter. Last night, we missed our end-of-month fundraising goal for August. We set a goal to raise $50,000 last month to ensure we have the resources to support our first slate of endorsements ahead of this November’s elections. In critical races across the country, a little extra support makes a world of difference. Falling short of our goal means making hard decisions about where and what to cut from our budget. But cutting back could mean MAGA megadonors getting ahead and drowning our Democratic candidates out — and we can’t let that happen, Peter. With exactly 9 weeks until the general election, I know we can still make up lost ground if we act now. This grassroots team has always shown up when it matters most. If we want to elect a new generation of leaders who will finally give our working-class communities the representation they deserve in Washington, I need supporters like you to step up today. I can’t thank you enough, Tim

name: Team AOC
subject: As the school year starts, will you donate to Learn To Be?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Students across the country are going back to school to start another academic year of learning and growing. 🎒✏️
We believe that every student should start the year off with their head held high which is why we organize a yearly backpack drive to distribute backpacks and supplies to students in New York City.
But once school starts, we know many students might struggle to complete homework or access tutoring services.
We believe that **money shouldn’t dictate access to education — all students deserve the resources to succeed.**
You may remember that our campaign launched a virtual tutoring program in 2020 called Homework Helpers to assist families with the demands of online learning during the pandemic. We were able to provide families across New York City with over 8,000 hours of virtual homework assistance.
In the Summer of 2023, we decided to transition the program to the educational non-profit Learn To Be, which has been providing free virtual tutoring to students across the country since 2008.
[ As kids are heading back to school, please donate $5 or more to Learn To Be, to support their work of offering free virtual tutoring to students from low-income families or in foster care.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260901-ltb.g5VJ41&refcode=em20260901-12210-P_FND_CHA_HWH&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12210%2E2526796%2E_KN5Xf)
**_100% of your donation will go to Learn To Be._ **
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260901-ltb.g5VJ41&refcode=em20260901-12210-P_FND_CHA_HWH&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=12210%2E2526796%2E_KN5Xf)**
Here are just a few testimonials from parents and tutors about Learn To Be’s positive impact:
> “I love Learn To Be because it provides wonderful academic support for my children. The platform is very easy to use, and we are so grateful for the amazing volunteer tutors who give their time to help our kids learn and succeed. Thank you for this wonderful program!”
> “Alice is an amazing reading tutor! She is highly dedicated and prepares her own custom slide presentations and special learning materials for my daughter. The lessons are incredibly lively, dynamic, and always full of great energy. She keeps my daughter fully engaged throughout the entire session. We are very grateful for her effort!”
> “It has been a wonderful experience working with Learn To Be, and I’m thankful for the opportunity to support students through the program.”
> “I love seeing the smile on my students' faces when they understand something new I teach them.”
**Every $5 donation funds one full hour of tutoring** and pays for the technology platform, tutor training, student matching, and ongoing support that makes Learn To Be’s tutoring possible.
[ A $25 donation today would cover 5 hours of one-on-one tutoring! Can you pitch in today?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260901-ltb.g5VJ41&refcode=em20260901-12210-P_FND_CHA_HWH&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=23&akid=12210%2E2526796%2E_KN5Xf)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260901-ltb.g5VJ41&refcode=em20260901-12210-P_FND_CHA_HWH&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=42&akid=12210%2E2526796%2E_KN5Xf)**
We’ve seen this movement step up to achieve incredible things before. Together we’ve raised millions for mutual aid groups, relief programs, and more.
Whether or not you can contribute today, thank you for standing with us.
In solidarity,
Team AOC

**[Donate](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260901-ltb.g5VJ41&refcode=em20260901-12210-P_FND_CHA_HWH&t=1&akid=12210%2E2526796%2E_KN5Xf)** | **[Merch](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/9251?utm_source=em-footer-20260901-12210-P_FND_CHA_HWH&t=2&akid=12210%2E2526796%2E_KN5Xf)**

| | | | | | Peter,
I need you to think about this number for a moment:
**387,000.**
That’s how many Pennsylvania households faced utility shutoffs last year. Not in a recession. Not during a natural disaster. In one of the wealthiest states in the richest country in the world, nearly 400,000 families couldn’t keep their lights on.
And in the same year, Pennsylvania’s average electricity cost went up almost 15%. The average electricity bill has gone up more than 20% since 2024. Another round of rate increases is hitting this summer.
**Where is Josh Shapiro on any of this?**
He’s the highest-paid governor in America. He presides over the 47th-ranked economy in the country. He has the 5th highest tax burden. And his response to a utility affordability crisis is — nothing.
He welcomed in out of state data center developers who are consuming massive amounts of electricity and driving up energy costs for everyone else. And his only energy “plan” is to hold press conferences.
**Press conferences don’t keep the lights on.**
Here’s what a Garrity Administration will do:
⚡ Cut utility bills by 15–25%
🏭 Fast-track new power generation so supply can meet the growing demand
🏠 Cut property taxes by one-third through the HOPE for PA initiative
387,000 families. That number should keep every elected official in Harrisburg up at night. Instead, the Governor is on a book tour.
**It’s time to turn Pennsylvania around.**
– Team Garrity

In a complaint filed with Senator Richard Blumenthal, an anonymous USPS official revealed that the agency built its Trump-ordered ballot-verification system so fast and so carelessly that, in the whistleblower's own words, **"catastrophic failure would be a feature rather than a bug."** Read that again. The system could send a ballot into repeated verification cycles and delay it indefinitely. **Multiply that by every mail voter in Oregon and you get a real possibility: millions of legitimate ballots, stuck,****_undelivered, in November._** Here's the timeline. The Supreme Court cleared a procedural hurdle for this rule on Monday. USPS rushed out its final version by Friday. Oregon and 23 other states sued again within days. A federal court has already slapped a temporary restraining order on most of it. We are winning the legal fights. We've beaten this administration in court twice already. name: Team Molly
subject: ⏰Big news⏰: Two major labor endorsements for Molly
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/MG%20LOGO%20-WEB%20%281%29.png]

Hi Peter,

We have some BIG news to share:

Molly just earned two major labor endorsements – from the Vermont-NEA and the Professional Firefighters of Vermont!

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/IMG_3033%202%20%281%29.JPG][https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/small%20kiddos.jpeg]

The Vermont-NEA is Vermont’s largest union by membership , representing approximately 13,000 educators and education professionals across our state.

The Professional Firefighters of Vermont represents career fire and EMS professionals from 13 organizations across Vermont.

These endorsements are a powerful show of support for Molly and the campaign we’re building together, and they come at an important moment as we head into the General Election.

When Molly met with the Vermont-NEA board on Saturday, she spoke about the importance of protecting rural schools and investing in the communities they anchor.

“When Molly said ‘when we close a rural school, we close that community,’ it was clear that the needs of students and our small towns are important to her,” said Don Tinney, president of Vermont-NEA.

And the firefighters recognized Molly’s commitment to public safety and working Vermonters, too:

“Molly has shown a commitment to supporting labor and public safety in Vermont. Molly has been visiting fire stations throughout Vermont to meet with our members and hear their concerns related to public safety and labor.”

This is what momentum looks like.

Educators. Firefighters. Working families. Rural communities.

More and more Vermonters are coming together behind Molly because they know she will fight to lower costs, fight to protect the fundamental rights of every Vermonter, make life better for working families, and make sure every Vermonter can live, work, and retire with dignity.

We’re so grateful to everyone who has helped us get here. And we’re just getting started!

Thank you for being part of this team,

Team Molly
